title: Adaptive Self-Organizing Neural Networks
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to neural network architecture – Adaptive Self-Organizing Neural Networks (ASON) – designed to automate the construction of complex network structures and enhance the efficiency of neural network training. Traditional neural network training often necessitates manual design, while ASON offers a method for automatically generating network topologies, thereby reducing the computational burden associated with training. The core of this algorithm lies in a dynamic adjustment of connection weights, enabling self-organizing network structure formation. This research explores the practical implications of this methodology through a detailed analysis and preliminary experimentation.

title: Self-Supervised Learning of Graph Embeddings with Contrastive Relational Prediction
abstract: Graph representation learning has emerged as a powerful technique for analyzing and understanding complex data structures represented as graphs. Existing self-supervised learning methods for graph embeddings frequently struggle to effectively capture intricate relational patterns within graphs. This work proposes a novel approach leveraging contrastive relational prediction to generate more informative graph embeddings. The core idea is to train a network to distinguish between similar and dissimilar relational pairs, effectively learning a richer representation of the graph's underlying relationships. We formulate the problem as a contrastive learning task, where positive pairs consist of related nodes and negative pairs consist of unrelated nodes based on defined relational structures. The model learns embeddings that maximize similarity between positive pairs and minimize similarity between negative pairs. This approach demonstrates improved performance in downstream graph tasks compared to existing methods, showcasing the effectiveness of contrastive learning for robust and expressive graph embedding. The key contributions of this work lie in the application of contrastive learning to the problem of graph embedding, resulting in embeddings that better capture relational structures.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Reasoning with Dynamic Bayesian Networks
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to neuro-symbolic reasoning utilizing Dynamic Bayesian Networks (DBNs). The core idea is to leverage the strengths of both neural networks and Bayesian networks, specifically addressing the complexities of dynamic knowledge representation. We introduce an architecture where a DBN serves as the foundational knowledge representation, and a neural network is trained to predict the transition probabilities within the DBN. This allows the system to learn and reason about uncertainty and causal relationships within the knowledge domain. The key innovation lies in the dynamic nature of the representation, enabling the system to adapt to changing environments and incorporate new information effectively. This approach offers improved robustness and flexibility compared to static neuro-symbolic systems. The paper outlines the architecture, the training methodology, and demonstrates the potential benefits of this combined approach through a theoretical framework. The proposed method offers a promising direction for building more intelligent and adaptable reasoning systems.

title: American Pika: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper introduces a new metaheuristic algorithm, the American Pika Algorithm (APA), inspired by the foraging behavior of American pikas (Ochotona princeps). Pikas are known for their efficient and adaptive foraging strategies in mountainous environments, selecting food sources based on a combination of factors including food quality, availability, and distance. The APA leverages these principles to develop a novel optimization algorithm. The algorithm utilizes a population-based search, represented by a set of pika agents, each exploring the search space based on a dynamically updated 'preference' vector, analogous to the pika's assessment of food quality. A 'risk aversion' mechanism, mirroring the pika's tendency to avoid overly risky food sources, is implemented to prevent premature convergence. The algorithm's core components include a local search operator based on a modified gradient descent, and a global search mechanism driven by a simulated 'territorial defense' behavior among pika agents. Performance evaluations are presented across a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating the APA's competitiveness against established metaheuristic algorithms. The key parameters of the APA are: *N* (population size), *K* (number of preference components), *α* (risk aversion coefficient), and *β* (exploration coefficient). The algorithm's efficiency and adaptability are discussed, highlighting its potential applications in diverse optimization challenges.

title: Graph Neural Networks for Software Architecture Design
abstract: This paper explores the application of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) to the domain of software architecture design. Traditional software architecture design heavily relies on human expertise and experience, often resulting in lengthy and complex design processes. This research proposes a novel approach leveraging GNNs to automatically generate software architecture designs. The core concept involves representing a software architecture as a graph, where nodes represent software components and edges represent their dependencies. GNNs are then employed to learn the structural features of these graphs and subsequently generate new architecture designs. This automated design process offers the potential for increased efficiency, reduced design time, and potentially, improved architectural quality. The presented framework provides a foundation for future research exploring the integration of GNNs within broader software engineering workflows.

title: Algorithmic Quantum State Collapse for Pattern Recognition
abstract: Quantum state collapse is a fascinating phenomenon in quantum mechanics, where a quantum system abruptly changes its state, seemingly instantaneously. This concept has garnered significant attention in recent years, particularly in the context of quantum computing and information theory. We propose an algorithmic approach to leverage this principle to enhance pattern recognition in high-dimensional data. The core mechanism involves designing a quantum state collapse process to induce a dynamic representation shift, facilitating the detection of subtle correlations that classical algorithms might miss. This paper explores the potential of this method, detailing the theoretical framework, proposed algorithm, and initial experimental investigations, aiming to demonstrate a significant improvement in pattern recognition performance.

This research aims to advance our understanding of quantum systems through the application of advanced mathematical tools and conceptual frameworks.

The core concept revolves around modeling quantum system evolution as a probabilistic process, utilizing topological structures to provide a deeper understanding of system dynamics. We propose a method for constructing a unified model capable of accurately predicting quantum phenomena, with a specific focus on the intricacies of quantum entanglement and state evolution, which are central to quantum computing. The proposed method addresses the limitations of existing probabilistic models by incorporating topological aspects, offering a more comprehensive and insightful approach to system simulation. This research aims to advance our understanding of quantum systems through the application of advanced mathematical tools and conceptual frameworks.

title: African Wood Mouse Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Wood Mouse Optimization Algorithm" (WMOA), inspired by the foraging behavior of African Wood Mice. These mice exhibit a remarkable ability to efficiently locate food sources in complex and dynamic environments. The WMOA leverages this innate intelligence by employing a combination of exploration and exploitation strategies mimicking the mouse's movement patterns and decision-making processes. The algorithm utilizes a population-based search approach, incorporating elements of Lévy flight, adaptive step sizes, and a novel "nesting" mechanism to guide the search towards promising solutions. The performance of the WMOA is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its efficacy in finding near-optimal solutions with reasonable computational cost. The key contributions of this work include the formulation of a new operator, the adaptive step size control, and the nesting mechanism, which are designed to enhance the algorithm's robustness and convergence speed. The algorithm's performance is compared with existing metaheuristic techniques, highlighting its strengths and weaknesses. Future research directions will focus on incorporating machine learning techniques to further refine the algorithm's parameters and adapt it to specific problem domains.

title: 基于自适应拓扑网络的量子态预测算法
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum state prediction algorithm based on an adaptive topology network. Traditional quantum state prediction methods often rely on static models, limiting their ability to accurately predict quantum state evolution. This algorithm leverages the dynamic nature of topology to achieve more efficient and adaptive state optimization. The core mechanism involves adjusting the topology structure dynamically, enabling a more nuanced and precise prediction of quantum states. We demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness through theoretical analysis and simulation, showcasing improvements in prediction accuracy and state optimization compared to existing approaches. The resulting system offers a significant step towards enhanced quantum control and manipulation.

title: Quantum State-Adaptive Geometry Optimization Algorithm
abstract: Quantum State-Adaptive Geometry Optimization Algorithm is a novel optimization algorithm designed to address challenges in optimizing complex geometric structures. This paper explores the application of quantum state properties to achieve high-precision optimization. We present a new approach that leverages the inherent adaptability of quantum states to guide the optimization process, offering a potential paradigm shift in the field of geometric optimization. The core mechanism centers on dynamically adjusting the geometric structure based on quantum state manipulations, leading to improved results compared to traditional methods. This work demonstrates the potential of quantum state manipulation for enhancing geometric optimization.

title: Dynamic State-Based Neuron Network Model
abstract: This research introduces a novel dynamic state-based neuron network model designed to emulate the intricate dynamics of biological neural systems. Traditional neural network models often struggle to represent the complex, dynamic nature of the brain, while this model offers a framework for learning and predicting biological signals through the incorporation of dynamic state representation. The core mechanism focuses on introducing a dynamic state concept, enabling the model to evolve and adapt to variations in biological neural activity. The model's architecture and training methodology are presented, highlighting its potential for improved biological signal interpretation and analysis.

title: Nonlinear Geometry-Driven Quantum Computing Optimization
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum computing optimization algorithm based on the integration of non-linear geometry functions. The core concept revolves around modeling quantum computation processes as non-linear geometric functions, allowing for automated adjustments to optimize quantum circuit parameters and overall system performance. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a detailed analysis and implementation of a specific optimization framework. The system's design prioritizes enhanced optimization efficiency and reduced reliance on manual parameter tuning, offering a significant advancement in quantum computing algorithm development.

title: Dynamic Topology Neural Networks: A Novel Approach to Enhanced Expressiveness and Generalization
abstract: This paper presents a novel neural network architecture, termed Dynamic Topology Neural Networks (DTN), designed to enhance both expressiveness and generalization capabilities. Traditional neural networks often rely on static, predetermined topologies, limiting their adaptability and potential for learning complex patterns. DTN leverages a dynamic topology structure, allowing the network's connections to adapt during training, effectively capturing and expressing more intricate relationships within the data. We explore the mechanisms through which this dynamic topology improves performance, focusing on the optimization of connection weights and the inherent adaptability of the network's representation. The work demonstrates improved performance across a range of benchmark datasets, highlighting the potential of this approach to address limitations inherent in standard neural network designs.

title: Title: Quantum Topological Verification via Hidden Computation
abstract: Quantum topological verification offers a novel approach to validating topological structures, addressing limitations of classical methods. This paper explores the application of quantum hidden computation to enhance the efficiency and accuracy of a topological verification algorithm. The core mechanism centers around exploiting the inherent properties of quantum computation to minimize computational complexity and reduce the reliance on computationally intensive operations. We present a detailed algorithm and demonstrate its effectiveness through a rigorous analysis of a specific topological structure. The research highlights the potential of quantum hidden computation to revolutionize the verification process, offering a promising avenue for improved results. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions and potential applications.

title: Uncanny Valley Responses to Generative AI-Based Short-Form Food Advertising ― Focusing on Consumer Experience by Production Method and Presentation Style ―
abstract: 본 연구는 숏폼 식품 광고에서 제작 방식과 연출 방식이 소비자 반응에 미치는 영향을 검토하였다. 이를 위해 실제 촬영 광고와 AI 생성 광고, 인물중심 광고와 비인물 중심 광고를 결합한 2×2 피험자 내 반복측정 실험을 수행하고, 151명의 응답을 분석하였다. 분석 결과, AI 생성 광고는 실제 촬영 광고보다 인지된 기괴함, 허위성 인식, 광고 불신도가 높고, 인지된 사실성, 인지된 창의성, 수용 의도는 낮게 나타났다. AI 생성 광고 내에서는 비인물 중심 광고가 인물 중심 광고보다 기괴함이 낮고 사실성과 창의성이 높게 평가되었다. 부가 분석 결과, 인지된 사실성은 수용 의도를 유의하게 직접 예측하였으나, 허위성 인식과 광고 불신도를 통한 간접 경로는 유의하지 않았다. 본 연구는 불쾌한 골짜기 이론을 AI 기반 식품 광고 연출 맥락으로 확장하고, 시각적 사실성과 인물 연출 방식이 소비자 수용에 미치는 차별적 영향을 실증함으로써 현 기술 수준의 생성형 AI 숏폼 식품 광고의 연출 디자인에 대한 이론적·실무적 기준을 제시한다.

title: An Efficient and Secure Framework for Enhancing Data and Model Security in Healthcare AI
abstract: The Artificial Intelligence (AI) enabled healthcare systems are require simultaneous defense of complex patient data and of the trained models. The paper proposes a dual-layer security architecture that combines AES-256 data encryption, homomorphic encryption (HE) for model protection, role-based access control (RBAC) with multi-factor authentication (MFA) and the digital watermarking for model ownership verification. The outline is evaluated on the MIMIC-III clinical dataset using a feedforward neural network for healthcare prediction. The experimental results show a test accuracy of 92.53%, data encryption and decryption times of 0.144s and 0.109s, model-level encryption and decryption times of 0.0019s and 0.0002s with a watermark tamper resistance of 99.95% under simulated adversarial attack. Compared with three recent baseline frameworks, the proposed approach achieves the highest tamper resistance and the fastest encryption or decryption operations the outperforms the layered cryptographic and access-control mechanisms as embedded into an AIML pipeline without the compromising low latency requirements of real world clinical deployment.

title: When and What to Teach: Budget-Aware Online Adaptation for Web Agents
abstract: Web agents have achieved significant success in automating complex internet tasks but deploying them in real-world environments requires continuous online adaptation. Given that deploying powerful proprietary models remains commercially cost-prohibitive, practitioners must rely on lightweight local models that evolve post-deployment via online teaching from a stronger teacher. However, standard interactive feedback imposes prohibitive costs. We show that conventional trajectory-level preference optimization wastes budget on both unresolvable episodes and redundant execution turns. To resolve these inefficiencies, we propose \textbf{Score-Guided Online Teaching with Budgeted Trajectory Trimming}, a budget-aware framework that systematically orchestrates \textbf{when} and \textbf{what} to teach. Specifically, our framework integrates a solvability-aware teacher gate to dictate \textbf{when} to query the teacher model and a score-guided turn selection mechanism to decide \textbf{what} informative turns to retain. Extensive experiments on MiniWoB and TimeWarp demonstrate that our method achieves comparable first-pass success while reducing teacher calls by 22.6\% and student training compute by 52.1\% on average. Our code is available at https://github.com/zjw131f1fc/budgeted-online-teaching.

title: IMPACT: Attention Is the Interaction Map for Scalable Interaction-Aware World Model Training
abstract: World models have made remarkable progress in action-conditioned future prediction for embodied agents, yet still struggle to model physically plausible interactions. Existing approaches address this limitation by constraining the generation process with external representations encoding motion, geometry, or semantics. Obtaining these spatiotemporally dense representations typically requires auxiliary estimators or manual annotations, limiting training scalability. We instead revisit the training objective and identify a supervision-allocation mismatch under the globally averaged mean squared error (MSE) denoising objective: prevalent static content dominates the optimization signal, leaving sparse dynamic-object regions critical to interaction generation disproportionately under-supervised. Motivated by this observation, we introduce IMPACT, a scalable Interaction-aware Model training framework with Prior-guided Attention Calibration and Targeting. IMPACT uses cross-attention associated with manipulated-object tokens as an internal spatiotemporal prior for action-conditioned changes. It samples candidate regions from this prior, calibrates them with detached local prediction errors to construct an interaction map, and uses the map to reweight denoising supervision, requiring neither external representations nor inference-time modifications. Extensive experiments on robot-arm and human-hand manipulation, spanning diverse control modalities and DiT backbones, show that IMPACT consistently outperforms the corresponding MSE-trained baselines, improving interaction fidelity, physical plausibility, and visual quality.

title: TUE-Detector: A Tool-Using Expert MLLM-Based Detector for AI-Generated Videos
abstract: AI-generated video detection, which aims to distinguish AI-generated videos from real ones, has recently received increasing research attention. To perform this task reliably, a key challenge lies in accurately identifying subtle-yet-measurable unnatural artifacts. In this work, we address this challenge from a novel perspective of tool-mediated evidence discovery and propose Tool-Using Expert MLLM-based AI-generated Video Detector (TUE-Detector), a novel framework for AI-generated video detection. TUE-Detector trains a general MLLM into a task-tailored tool-using expert detector that learns to invoke suitable tools, collect concrete evidence of unnaturalness, and reason over the evidence for reliable detection. Meanwhile, TUE-Detector further introduces novel designs to equip the expert detector with high-quality and suitable tools. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our framework.

title: Textual Acoustic Grounding for Generalizable LLM-Based Deepfake Voice Detection
abstract: Deepfake voice detection suffers from poor generalization across unseen domains. While Audio Large Language Models (ALLMs) show promise, the modality gap between continuous audio embeddings which capture the subtle acoustic details necessary for deepfake detection and the semantic space of LLMs remains a critical, underexplored bottleneck. We address this by benchmarking diverse audio encoders integrated with Qwen LLMs (0.5B to 7B parameters). First, we demonstrate that fine-tuning the LLM alone risks out-of-domain overfitting, making a frozen LLM a stronger, resource-efficient baseline. Second, to explicitly bridge the modality gap, we introduce a cross-modal prompting strategy that injects linguistic-knowledge-driven acoustic features (via openSMILE) as structured text tokens. This explicit textual grounding not only enhances the frozen baseline but also makes LLM fine-tuning more effective. Ultimately, our approach demonstrates state-of-the-art resilience on the out-of-domain ITW and MLAAD benchmarks, yielding over \textbf{16.2\%} absolute improvement in Macro-F1 over existing ALLM baselines while maintaining competitive in-domain performance. All models reported in this work are \href{https://huggingface.co/01Yassine/AudioLLM-Deepfake-Detection}{publicly available}.

title: Robótica educativa wedo y regulación emocional de estudiantes de secundaria de una Institución Educativa Lima 2025
abstract: La indagación tuvo como propósito establecer la conexión entre la robótica educativa WeDo y la regulación emocional en escolares de secundaria de un colegio de Lima 2025. Se buscó sustentar la robótica educativa y la regulación emocional como recursos que promueven el desarrollo emocional y fortalecen los procesos de enseñanza-aprendizaje. Fue de bosquejo cuantitativo, tipo básico y diseño no empírico, transversal y descriptivocorrelacional. El ejemplar fue de 249 escolares. Se aplicó dos cuestionarios uno para cada variable. Se concluyó que hay conexión directa y relevante entre la robótica educativa WeDo y la regulación de emociones en los escolares de secundaria de una escuela de Lima, 2025 con una correspondencia mediano con rho=409, p-valor=0.000<0.05 y r2=0.167. Quiere decir que mayor grado de utilización de la robótica educativa WeDo mayor será su regulación emocional en los estudiantes.

title: Quantum Entanglement Computing: Adaptive Protocol Design
abstract: Quantum entanglement computing holds immense potential for transformative computational capabilities, exceeding the limitations of classical computing. This paper explores the design of a novel adaptive protocol for quantum entanglement computation, focusing on the ability to dynamically adjust entangled states to achieve enhanced parallelism and computational efficiency. We propose a mechanism leveraging a hybrid state approach, allowing for flexible entanglement manipulation and subsequent, coordinated quantum operations. The core claim centers on the capability of this protocol to surpass classical computation through the utilization of entangled states. We detail the proposed protocol's architecture, discuss its key advantages, and outline future research directions.

abstract: This research investigates the potential of adaptive quantum entanglement to enhance probabilistic analysis in quantum computing and quantum communication. This approach overcomes limitations of traditional quantum algorithms by directly incorporating the inherent probabilistic properties of entangled systems. The study explores the benefits of this framework in enhancing quantum error correction and enabling more efficient quantum computations. The findings will provide a foundation for advanced quantum algorithms and protocols.

title: Title: Geometric Proof of Concept for Quantum Error Correction
abstract: Quantum error correction is a critical challenge in quantum computing, requiring robust protection against errors that can compromise computation. Traditional error correction methods often rely on local manipulations, which can be complex and resource-intensive. This paper presents a geometric proof of concept demonstrating the feasibility of achieving quantum error correction using a novel geometric framework. We introduce a 'Geometric Error Signature' – a mathematical measure quantifying the impact of errors – and propose a geometric transformation that guides the correction process. This approach offers a fundamentally new perspective on error correction, potentially enabling more efficient and scalable solutions. The paper details the implementation of this geometric framework and provides preliminary results demonstrating its effectiveness in guiding quantum state correction.

abstract: Quantum algorithms, renowned for their potential to solve complex problems beyond the capabilities of classical computation, often face limitations in terms of efficiency and generalization. title: Based on Genetic Algorithm Hardware Design Optimization
abstract: This paper investigates the application of a genetic algorithm (GA) to optimize the design of hardware circuits. Traditional hardware design methodologies often rely heavily on human expertise and iterative refinement, leading to inefficiencies and subjective outcomes. This research proposes a novel approach where the hardware design process is formulated as an optimization problem suitable for GA. The core claim of this work is that GA can effectively enhance circuit performance and reduce power consumption through automated design exploration. The methodology involves representing circuit designs as chromosomes within a GA population, employing fitness functions to evaluate design quality, and utilizing genetic operators such as crossover and mutation to drive the search for optimal solutions. The presented framework offers a systematic and potentially more efficient method for hardware design compared to conventional techniques. The paper details the design process, including chromosome representation, fitness function definition, and GA parameter tuning, and concludes with a discussion of potential applications and future research directions. ---

title: Dynamic Neuron Topology Network Self-Assembly
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to neural network design and optimization through dynamic neuron topology network self-assembly. The core concept involves mimicking the biological processes of neuronal growth and connection, leading to networks with adaptive topology and complex functionality. We employ reinforcement learning to simulate synaptic connections and inhibition between neurons, combined with topology optimization algorithms to guide the network's self-organization into more efficient and robust connection patterns. These patterns are dynamically adjusted based on environmental feedback. Unlike traditional neural network training methods that rely on pre-defined topologies, our approach enables autonomous learning and optimization of network structure, representing a fundamental shift in the design paradigm. The proposed method offers potential advantages in terms of adaptability, robustness, and the ability to tackle complex problems that are difficult for conventional neural networks to solve. The key mathematical framework utilizes concepts from graph theory, reinforcement learning, and topology optimization, resulting in a dynamic network architecture that can evolve and adapt to changing conditions. The presented architecture aims to achieve superior performance compared to static networks by leveraging the inherent flexibility of a self-assembling system.

title: Formal Program Semantic Embedding and Proof
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to program verification by formally embedding program semantics into a formal semantic model and subsequently leveraging formal methods to prove program correctness. The core idea is to establish a new program semantic model based on type theory and dependent types, achieving precise correspondence between program code and formal semantics. This model then facilitates program verification through formal reasoning systems. We demonstrate the potential of this approach to significantly enhance program reliability and provide a rigorous methodology for program validation. The central mechanism involves translating program constructs into their corresponding formal representations within the defined semantic model, followed by applying automated theorem proving techniques to derive proof obligations. The resulting system offers a pathway toward reducing software errors and increasing developer confidence. ---

title: Graph Embedding-Based Software Architecture Design
abstract: This paper explores the application of graph embedding techniques to software architecture design. Traditional software architecture design methods often face challenges in efficiently capturing complex relationships and dependencies within systems. Graph embedding offers a novel approach by representing software architectures as graphs and leveraging embedding algorithms to learn latent feature representations. These learned representations can then be utilized to inform architectural decisions, optimize system design, and potentially automate aspects of the design process. This work details the methodology, presents key findings, and argues for the significant potential of graph embedding in revolutionizing how software architectures are conceived and implemented. The core claim is that utilizing graph embedding technology to model and analyze software architectures improves the efficiency and quality of software architecture design. The core mechanism involves representing software architecture as a graph structure, employing graph embedding algorithms to learn architectural features, and then basing design decisions on the results of the graph embeddings.

title: Black-Backed Shrew Mole: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Black-Backed Shrew Mole" (BBSM), inspired by the foraging strategies of the black-backed shrew mole ( *Talpa caeca* ). The algorithm leverages the animal's efficient and adaptive search behavior for complex optimization problems. BBSM employs a combination of particle swarm optimization (PSO) and a simulated annealing (SA) framework, incorporating a 'memory' mechanism mimicking the shrew mole's ability to remember favorable foraging locations. The algorithm's core components include a dynamic velocity update rule influenced by both global and local best positions, a temperature schedule mimicking the shrew mole's sensitivity to environmental changes, and a 'memory' component that biases the search towards previously successful locations. We demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, showing its competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic methods. The key innovations of BBSM lie in its adaptive memory mechanism and the integration of SA's temperature adaptation with the PSO framework, resulting in improved convergence speed and solution quality. The algorithm's performance is evaluated based on convergence rate, solution accuracy, and computational efficiency.

title: Information-Theoretic Limits of Quantum Neural Networks
abstract: This paper investigates the fundamental limits of quantum neural networks (QNNs) from an information-theoretic perspective. We derive a precise bound on the representational capacity of QNNs, encompassing both classical and quantum information processing. The analysis utilizes Shannon entropy and related measures to quantify information storage and transmission within the network. The core contribution lies in providing a rigorous framework for understanding the inherent constraints on QNN performance, which can inform the design and optimization of these networks. We explore scenarios involving various quantum information processing techniques and demonstrate how they impact the achievable information capacity. The results highlight the crucial role of quantum entanglement and superposition in expanding representational capabilities, while also identifying potential bottlenecks arising from information loss and decoherence. Ultimately, this work establishes a foundational understanding of the information-theoretic limits governing the development of practical and powerful QNNs.

title: Adaptive Kernel Learning for Metric Space Clustering
abstract: This paper presents an adaptive kernel learning approach for metric space clustering, addressing the limitations of traditional kernel methods that rely on manually tuned kernel parameters. The core idea is to dynamically adjust the kernel function during the clustering process, leveraging reinforcement learning to optimize its influence based on local data density and cluster shape characteristics. Unlike conventional methods that fix kernel parameters a priori, this adaptive approach allows the algorithm to learn the most suitable kernel function for a specific dataset, ultimately leading to enhanced clustering accuracy. The proposed method utilizes a state representation encompassing local density estimations and cluster shape descriptors, which are then used to guide the reinforcement learning agent's selection of kernel parameters. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through theoretical analysis and illustrate its potential with a conceptual framework. The primary contribution lies in the automated discovery of optimal kernel functions, removing the burden of parameter tuning and significantly improving clustering performance in diverse scenarios.

This work details the core mechanism of the Self-Adaptive Quantum Corrector, its benefits, and potential applications.

title: 基于神经符号AI的知识图谱推理
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to knowledge graph reasoning leveraging the strengths of neural networks and symbolic reasoning. The core idea is to integrate these two paradigms, creating a system capable of performing complex knowledge graph inferences. We introduce a framework where a neural network learns patterns and relationships within the knowledge graph, and a symbolic reasoning engine handles logical and deductive reasoning. The synergistic interaction between these components enables a deeper understanding of the knowledge graph and facilitates knowledge discovery. This research addresses limitations in traditional knowledge graph reasoning techniques by combining the pattern recognition capabilities of neural networks with the precise logical deduction of symbolic systems. The proposed system aims to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of knowledge graph inferences, particularly in scenarios involving incomplete or uncertain information. The key contributions lie in the architecture and the methodology for effectively bridging the gap between neural and symbolic representations, leading to a more robust and intelligent knowledge graph reasoning system.

title: Based on Multi-Agent Collaborative Learning for Program Synthesis
abstract: This paper explores the potential of multi-agent collaborative learning (M-ACL) for program synthesis, aiming to automate the generation of more complex and efficient programs. Traditional program synthesis approaches often struggle with the inherent complexity of generating robust and optimized code. We propose a system composed of multiple "program synthesis agents," each specialized in a specific aspect of the synthesis process – such as algorithm selection, code optimization, and test generation. These agents interact through reinforcement learning (RL) and imitation learning (IL), fostering a dynamic and evolving process of program generation. The core innovation lies in leveraging the collective intelligence of these agents, overcoming the limitations of single-agent systems and enabling self-organization and evolutionary improvement in the generated programs. We present a framework for this M-ACL approach and discuss its potential applications and future research directions. ---

title: Non-Euclidean Probability Networks

The core of the system involves a continuous, non-linear mapping that adapts to the input data, rather than relying on fixed, predetermined distributions. This approach offers the potential for a much deeper and more flexible modeling capacity compared to conventional methods. We detail the network architecture, introduce a novel loss function, and present preliminary results demonstrating the potential for enhanced statistical accuracy and a qualitatively different type of probabilistic modeling.

title: Quantum Random Walk Algorithms for Feature Extraction
abstract: This paper explores the application of quantum random walks (QRWs) to feature extraction from high-dimensional data. Classical random walks often struggle with the curse of dimensionality, leading to inefficient exploration of the data space. QRWs, leveraging the inherent randomness of quantum mechanics, offer a potential solution by enabling more efficient exploration and potentially uncovering hidden correlations. This work details the theoretical framework for implementing QRWs on graph-based representations of data, presenting algorithms for both discrete and continuous graphs. We investigate the key differences between classical and quantum random walks, focusing on the role of superposition and entanglement in expanding the search space. The core claim is that QRWs can be utilized to extract meaningful features from high-dimensional data. We provide a mathematical formulation for analyzing the convergence and efficiency of QRWs, demonstrating the potential advantages over traditional methods. The paper concludes with a discussion on the challenges and future directions for this emerging field.

HCI-ASA incorporates three key mechanisms: a dynamic neighborhood structure mimicking the crab's shell selection, an adaptive step size control simulating environmental changes, and a probabilistic acceptance criterion reflecting the crab's decision-making process. The algorithm aims to achieve robust and efficient convergence in various optimization problems. This paper outlines the algorithm's design, theoretical considerations, and potential applications.

title: Annamese Langur-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (ALMA)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, Annamese Langur-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (ALMA), motivated by the foraging behavior of the Annamese langur, a primate known for its intricate movement patterns and efficient resource utilization. ALMA incorporates elements of the langur's adaptive strategies, particularly its ability to dynamically adjust search space and prioritize promising areas, into a new iterative optimization process. The algorithm utilizes a novel adaptive mutation operator based on the langur's jumping range and direction changes. The core of ALMA lies in a dynamic probability distribution function (PDF) that governs the exploration and exploitation phases, adapting to the landscape's complexity. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a set of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions within a reasonable timeframe. The key contributions of this work are the introduction of a biologically inspired adaptive mutation operator and a dynamic PDF, offering a potentially robust and efficient approach to tackling complex optimization challenges. The algorithm's performance is compared against established metaheuristic algorithms like Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) to showcase its advantages in certain scenarios. The results highlight the potential of mimicking natural behaviors for designing effective optimization methods.

title: # Andean Laucha: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Andean Laucha
abstract: This paper presents Andean Laucha, a novel metaheuristic algorithm designed for solving complex optimization problems. Inspired by the Andean Laucha, a remarkable rodent known for its adaptive foraging strategies and resilience in challenging environments, the algorithm leverages principles of exploration and exploitation to achieve efficient convergence. Andean Laucha integrates elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Simulated Annealing (SA), incorporating a novel 'Laucha-Adaptation' mechanism that dynamically adjusts exploration and exploitation parameters based on the algorithm's performance within the search space. The core of the algorithm rests on a modified velocity update rule in PSO, coupled with a temperature adjustment scheme inspired by the Laucha's behavioral responses to environmental changes. We demonstrate the effectiveness of Andean Laucha through simulations on benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its competitive performance against established metaheuristic algorithms. The algorithm's adaptability and ability to handle diverse problem landscapes are highlighted, suggesting its potential applicability across a broad range of optimization tasks. Key performance metrics, including convergence rate, solution quality, and computational efficiency, are thoroughly analyzed.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Algorithm Design
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum entanglement to revolutionize algorithm design, specifically focusing on the development of a novel algorithm paradigm centered on subtle correlations. We propose a 'Quantum Momentum' modifier, leveraging entanglement to guide the evolution of a solution space, offering significantly enhanced convergence speeds compared to traditional optimization techniques. The core mechanism hinges on the principle that entangled particles can subtly influence the system's trajectory, enabling faster and more efficient optimization. This research investigates the theoretical underpinnings of this approach, outlines the proposed algorithm architecture, and discusses potential applications across various optimization domains. The paper concludes with a preliminary assessment of the feasibility and impact of this quantum-inspired optimization strategy.

title: Quantum State-Based Dynamic Probability Model Optimization (QSPMO)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic probability model optimization algorithm, QSPMO, which leverages quantum state representations to dynamically adjust probability model parameters, leading to improved model prediction accuracy. Traditional probabilistic models often struggle with complex quantum systems due to their static nature. QSPMO addresses this limitation by employing quantum algorithms to iteratively refine probability parameter estimations based on the quantum state of the system. The core mechanism involves mapping the system's quantum state to a probabilistic representation, and then utilizing quantum optimization techniques to minimize the error between predicted and actual outcomes. This approach offers a promising pathway for enhancing predictive capabilities in various quantum applications.

abstract: This paper introduces the Non-linear Self-Organizing Neural Network Model (NSNQN) – a novel framework for quantum computing that leverages the principles of self-organization and quantum entanglement to simulate complex biological neural systems. Traditional neural networks often struggle to capture the intricate self-organization observed in biological neurons, limiting their ability to model intricate biological processes. The NSNQN utilizes quantum entanglement to enable self-learning and adaptive network behavior, offering a pathway toward advanced quantum computing applications. title: Dynamic Topology-Based Quantum State Generation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum state generation algorithm based on dynamic topology. Traditional quantum state generation methods often rely on static parameters, but this approach leverages the inherent complexity of topological structures to generate unique and potentially valuable quantum states. We propose a framework where the input is a topological structure, which is then manipulated through a dynamic process to produce a state exhibiting complex topology. The algorithm's core mechanism centers around the continuous application of a 'topology transformation' to the input, resulting in a state with a defined, but ever-evolving, topological shape. This allows for the exploration of quantum states with intricate and unpredictable properties, offering a significant departure from conventional techniques. We present preliminary results demonstrating the algorithm's effectiveness in generating specific quantum states, highlighting its potential for advancing quantum information theory and quantum computation.

title: Title: Adaptive Constraint-Based Probability Theory for Complex Systems
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative probabilistic theory, Adaptive Constraint-Based Probability Theory (ACPT), designed to address the challenges of predicting outcomes in complex systems. Traditional constraint-based models, while valuable, often struggle with dynamic environments and require manual adjustment. ACPT dynamically adapts constraint-based models in real-time, leveraging a self-modifying constraint system to improve prediction accuracy across a broad range of scenarios. The core mechanism involves a feedback loop that continuously refines the model based on observed data, ensuring robustness and adaptability. This research explores the potential of ACPT to overcome limitations of existing approaches and contribute to more reliable predictions in complex systems modeling.

title: ## The Rainbow Finch Inspired Adaptive Search Algorithm (RFA-SA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Rainbow Finch Inspired Adaptive Search Algorithm (RFA-SA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of the rainbow finch ( *Pyrrhura rhodopleur* ). The algorithm leverages the finch's ability to dynamically adjust its search strategy based on environmental factors – primarily food availability and its perceived distance from optimal locations – to achieve efficient exploration and exploitation. RFA-SA incorporates adaptive parameter control, mimicking the finch's instinctual responses, and utilizes a novel 'resonance' mechanism to enhance convergence. The core components include an adaptive search space expansion, a dynamic probability assignment system influenced by environmental "noise," and a resonance function that promotes convergence towards promising regions. This paper details the algorithm's design, its underlying principles, and its potential applications in various optimization problems. The focus is on the algorithm's theoretical framework and its conceptual alignment with the observed behaviors of the rainbow finch.

title: The Mimicry Optimization Algorithm: Inspired by the Behavior of the Speckle Woodpecker
abstract: This paper introduces the Mimicry Optimization Algorithm (MOA), a novel metaheuristic optimization technique inspired by the foraging behavior of the speckle woodpecker (Dendropentapus senegalensis). Speckle woodpeckers exhibit a remarkable ability to mimic the calls of other bird species, enhancing their foraging success. MOA leverages this mimicry strategy by iteratively adjusting a population of candidate solutions based on their similarity to the 'best' solution in the current generation, coupled with a random perturbation mechanism mimicking the woodcutter's exploration. The algorithm maintains a 'master' solution and a 'learner' solution, dynamically adjusting their parameters to optimize the overall population fitness. This paper details the algorithm's core principles, mathematical formulation, and potential applications, laying the groundwork for future research and development.

title: ## Alaskan Hare: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Hare Behavior
abstract: This paper introduces Alaskan Hare, a novel metaheuristic algorithm designed to address complex optimization problems. The algorithm is inspired by the foraging behavior of Alaskan hares, particularly their strategic movement patterns and resource exploitation. Alaskan Hare combines elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) with a novel adaptation mechanism based on hare's response to environmental changes. The algorithm utilizes a dynamic population size and adaptive inertia weight to enhance exploration and exploitation capabilities. We demonstrate the effectiveness of Alaskan Hare through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its ability to converge to optimal or near-optimal solutions with improved efficiency compared to traditional metaheuristics. The core of the algorithm lies in its "hare-inspired" movement strategy, which adjusts particle velocities and positions based on the perceived density of resources, mimicking a hare's decision-making process. The performance of Alaskan Hare is evaluated using metrics such as convergence rate, solution quality, and computational efficiency. Keywords: Metaheuristic, Optimization, Particle Swarm Optimization, Artificial Bee Colony, Hare Behavior, Dynamic Population, Adaptive Inertia Weight.

title: ## Alaska Marmot: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Marmot Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Alaska Marmot, a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of Alaskan marmots. Marmots exhibit a unique strategy of alternating between exploratory and exploitative phases, effectively balancing the need to discover new promising regions of the search space with the desire to refine solutions within already identified good areas. Alaska Marmot leverages this behavior through a dynamically adjusted exploration-exploitation balance, controlled by a novel "Marmot Phase Factor" (MPF). The algorithm employs a population-based approach, utilizing a swarm of potential solutions and iteratively refining them based on a fitness function. The MPF governs the frequency and intensity of exploratory moves, influencing the overall convergence behavior. We demonstrate the effectiveness of Alaska Marmot through simulations on benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its ability to outperform several established metaheuristic algorithms, particularly in problems with complex landscapes and multimodal solutions. The key innovations of this algorithm lie in its adaptive MPF and its ability to effectively navigate diverse optimization challenges.

title: Title: Contextual Graph Embedding for Semantic Reasoning
abstract: This paper introduces a novel method for representing knowledge and reasoning utilizing contextual graph embeddings. The core concept is to construct a "contextual graph" – a graph specifically designed to model relationships between concepts within a given scene or problem. This approach shifts the focus from isolated knowledge representations to a dynamic, interconnected system that facilitates more accurate and efficient semantic reasoning. The method leverages a unique graph structure to capture nuanced relationships and improve the performance of reasoning tasks. We present a framework for generating these contextual graphs and demonstrate its effectiveness through several benchmark problems, highlighting its potential to advance the field of knowledge representation and reasoning.

evidence.title: Allied Rock Wallaby: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of Allied Rock Wallabies
evidence.abstract: This paper presents Allied Rock Wallaby (ARW), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging strategies of Allied Rock Wallabies (Petrogale sphenistus). These wallabies are renowned for their efficient and adaptable foraging behavior in challenging, rocky terrain. ARW leverages the principles of exploration and exploitation observed in the wallabies' movements, combining elements of particle swarm optimization (PSO) and simulated annealing (SA) to create a robust and adaptive optimization technique. The algorithm utilizes a 'territory' concept, mirroring the wallabies' established feeding grounds, and incorporates a dynamic 'exploration radius' influenced by terrain complexity, mimicking their cautious movement and opportunistic search. Mathematical formulations detailing the core mechanics of ARW, including the territory assignment, exploration radius adjustment, and convergence criteria, are provided. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through a series of benchmark functions, demonstrating its effectiveness in solving complex optimization problems. title: Adaptive Geometry Transformation Parameter Adjustment Quantum Simulation
abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive quantum simulation parameter adjustment method for geometric transformations, leveraging quantum entanglement and superposition to dynamically adjust transformation parameters for improved simulation accuracy and efficiency. Existing quantum simulation techniques often rely on fixed parameter settings, limiting the potential for optimization. This work proposes a novel approach that utilizes quantum entanglement to create a dynamically evolving parameter space, allowing for a more nuanced and responsive simulation. The core mechanism centers around exploiting the inherent properties of quantum states to achieve a more accurate and efficient representation of geometric transformations. We present a theoretical framework and initial experimental validation demonstrating the efficacy of this method, highlighting its potential to significantly advance the field of quantum simulation.

title: Künstliche Intelligenz innerhalb der Due Diligence bei Mergers and Acquisitions
abstract: Künstliche Intelligenz innerhalb der Due Diligence bei Mergers and Acquisitions: Wie sich durch künstliche Intelligenz die Due Diligence verändert. Die zunehmende Digitalisierung und der Einsatz Künstlicher Intelligenz (KI) verändern die M&A-Landschaft maßgeblich. Vor allem die Due Diligence bietet durch die Analyse großer Datenmengen erhebliches Potenzial für den Einsatz von KI-Systemen. Ziel dieser Masterarbeit ist es, den aktuellen Einsatz von KI in der Due Diligence zu untersuchen. Zudem sollen wahrgenommene Potenziale und Risiken anhand des Implementierungsgrads empirisch untersucht werden. Hierzu wurde aufgrund des aktuellen Forschungsstands ein quantitatives Forschungsdesign entwickelt und eine Online-Befragung unter 91 Expert:innen aus Unternehmensberatungen, Banken, Wirtschaftskanzleien und Corporate-M&A-Abteilungen durchgeführt. Zur Auswertung wurden deskriptive Statistiken, Faktoranalysen und lineare Regressionsanalysen eingesetzt. Die Ergebnisse zeigen, dass hauptsächlich die Financial Due Diligence bereits durch KI unterstützt wird. Zudem konnte beobachtet werden, dass vor allem die Wahrnehmung von Potenzialen im Zusammenhang mit dem KI-Reifegrad einer Unternehmung hat. Gleichzeitig konnte kein Zusammenhang zur Wahrnehmung von Risiken festgestellt werden. Die Arbeit verdeutlicht, dass KI erhebliche Potenziale für die Automatisierung der Due Diligence bildet und diese Nutzenpotenziale bereits heute wahrgenommen werden. Zudem geht aus der Arbeit hervor, dass besonders eine starke IT-Infrastruktur wichtig ist.

title: Perceived Hallucination in Generative AI Travel Information and Tourists’ Verification, Trust, and Use Intention: An Information Behavior Theory Perspective
abstract: Purpose Based on Information Behavior Theory, this study aims to analyze the effects of perceived hallucination in generative AI travel information on tourists’ information verification behavior, information trust, and intention to use. In particular, this study empirically examines how AI hallucination perception affects the information use process, beyond being merely a negative perception, in situations where travel information provided by generative AI is used in tourists’ decision-making processes. Methods This study used 320 survey responses collected to measure perceptions of generative AI-based travel information. The data were analyzed using SPSS through frequency analysis, exploratory factor analysis, reliability analysis, correlation analysis, regression analysis, and mediation effect analysis. Results The results showed that perceived AI hallucination positively influenced information verification behavior, which in turn positively affected information trust. Information trust also had a positive effect on intention to use. Furthermore, the indirect effect of perceived AI hallucination on intention to use was significant through the sequential mediation of information verification behavior and information trust. Conclusion The findings suggest that, in the context of generative AI-based tourism information, perceived hallucination is not limited to undermining trust; rather, it may promote tourists’ active information verification behavior, which in turn contributes to the formation of information trust and intention to use.

title: Deterministic Minimum-Output-Entropy Nonadditivity via Haagerup's Inequality and Near-Free Permutation Representations
abstract: We give a deterministic realization of the finite-dimensional quadratic certificate underlying Collins's mixed-unitary proof of minimum-output-entropy nonadditivity. For every fixed integer $K\ge 2$ and rational $η>0$ satisfying $\log K>2(3+η)^2$, a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm, for every sufficiently large target size $N$, outputs $K$ permutations on $N'=N+o_{K,η}(N)$ points. Restricting their permutation matrices to the nontrivial standard representation yields real orthogonal Stinespring blocks and a channel $Φ_{N'}:M_{N'-1}(\mathbb{C})\to M_K(\mathbb{C})$ such that \[ 2H_{\min}(Φ_{N'}) -H_{\min}(Φ_{N'}^{\otimes 2}) \ge \frac{\log K}{K} -2\log\left(1+\frac{(3+η)^2}{K}\right) >0. \] The construction combines Haagerup's length-two inequality with the simultaneous deterministic spectral approximation of O'Donnell and Wu. We further show that the constant $3$ is asymptotically sharp on the relevant Hermitian zero-diagonal coefficient class and that the finite spectral transfer is nearly saturated, thereby isolating the finer geometry of the full output body as the natural next level of refinement beyond the scalar-radius method. Finally, a standard covariant extension converts the same deterministic entropy gap exactly into self-tensor superadditivity of the one-shot Holevo quantity.

title: Nonparametric Contextual Pricing and Inventory Learning under Censored Demand
abstract: In online retailing, when a product sells out, a retailer often sees only the units sold, not how many customers would have bought it had inventory been available. However, the inventory level determines how much demand is revealed, and this information can influence subsequent decisions and future profits. We study an online selling problem in which, in each round, the seller observes a market context and then makes pricing and stocking decisions based on censored sales data from previous rounds. The challenge is to learn a context-dependent pricing and stocking policy without assuming a particular formula for demand or observing realized profit. To overcome this difficulty, we propose a Mean-Calibrated Kernel UCB (MCK-UCB) algorithm that turns each incomplete sales record into a reliable guide for both inventory and price decisions, using data from past rounds with similar market conditions. This design allows us to learn while serving customers, without a separate exploration phase or the need to recover all demand hidden by stockouts. We prove the minimax optimality of the proposed algorithm, with strictly faster rates when expected profit varies more smoothly with price. Comprehensive numerical experiments have been conducted to confirm the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm.

title: SeqAlign3DVG: A Sequence-Aligned Benchmark and Voxel Reasoning Framework for 3D Visual Grounding
abstract: Image-based 3D visual grounding is critical for embodied agents, yet existing benchmarks suffer from loose text-observation alignment and neglect temporal ordering. We introduce SeqAlign3DVG, a novel benchmark dedicated to temporally ordered and strictly observation-aligned image-based 3D visual grounding. Unlike prior works using order-agnostic views or global point clouds, SeqAlign3DVG ensures all expressions are human-verified and strictly grounded in the provided RGB observations (single frames or ordered observation sequences). It comprises 9,622 single-view and 14,493 sequence samples featuring rich descriptions, complex relations, and multi-instance ambiguities. To tackle this benchmark, we propose a unified voxel-based pipeline featuring Relevance-Ordered Voxel Memory (ROVM) and Progressive Language-Voxel Fusion (PLVF). ROVM dynamically ranks and aggregates multi-view evidence via a conservative memory to mitigate noisy observations, while PLVF performs coarse-to-fine spatial-linguistic reasoning for precise disambiguation. Our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance under the depth-free protocol, significantly improving localization for targets defined by complex relations and appearance cues.

title: Using Prosody to Predict Syntactic Structure
abstract: While it is well-established that prosody carries crucial cues for syntactic structure, the degree and nature of correspondence between these two domains remains contested. We investigate the syntax-prosody interface through an information-theoretic lens, quantifying the interaction between prosodic features and syntactic representations as their mutual information. We provide a general-purpose framework for estimating this quantity over large speech-text corpora using multimodal language models. Our framework is structure-agnostic and modular, insofar as it can be used to measure the contributions of individual prosodic features or components of structure. We evaluate the syntax-prosody relationship for two features (word duration and inter-word pauses) across two domains--read audiobooks and spontaneous conversations--both in English. Our results demonstrate that prosody contains measurable syntactic information, with prosodic features reducing syntactic uncertainty in spontaneous conversations by up to 10.2%. Our findings offer new empirical support for several theoretical accounts of the syntax-prosody interface.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Financial Decision-Making: Opportunities, Risks, and Challenges
abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) has moved from a peripheral analytics tool to a core input in financial decision-making, shaping how institutions optimize portfolios, price risk, detect fraud, advise clients, and execute trades. This paper synthesizes recent academic literature, regulatory reports, and industry surveys (2020–2026) to examine the dual nature of AI adoption in finance: the strategic opportunities it creates and the risks and challenges it introduces. The review finds that AI materially improves predictive accuracy, operational efficiency, and access to financial services, with adoption accelerating sharply since the introduction of generative and agentic AI tools. At the same time, the literature converges on a consistent set of concerns: limited model explainability, algorithmic bias, cybersecurity and deepfake-enabled fraud, data privacy exposure, concentration and systemic risk from AI "monocultures," and a regulatory environment that has not kept pace with deployment. The paper presents a classification of AI application domains and associated risk categories, supported by quantitative adoption and market-growth data, and proposes a governance framework combining explainable AI, human oversight, and coordinated regulation. It concludes by identifying research gaps around long-term market stability effects, emerging-market adoption, and the governance of autonomous (agentic) financial AI. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence, Financial Decision-Making, Risk Management, Algorithmic Trading, Explainable AI, Financial Regulation, Agentic AI

title: Silicon Sample Benchmark — Tier 3 (direct effect forecast) submission (team team_28)
abstract: This Tier 3 entry uses a literature-conditioned multi-model ensemble to directly forecast treatment effects. The ensemble combines predictions from GPT-4o, GPT-5.4, Claude Sonnet 4.6, and Qwen3.8-27B. Qwen3.8-27B contributes two HippoRAG-based prediction series: one using the standard HippoRAG ranking and one using PIT-normalized fusion of 0.7 × graph and 0.3 × dense retrieval. The two Qwen series are averaged first, after which the four model-level prediction series are combined with equal weight. All predictions are calibrated and reported as average treatment effects for 16 interventions across 13 outcomes.

title: Fixed-K Speculative Decoding vs. EAGLE-3: A Like-for-Like, Energy-Measured Comparison in vLLM and SGLang
abstract: Benchmark code, raw telemetry and paper for a like-for-like comparison of fixed-window draft-model speculative decoding (Llama-3.2-1B drafting K=5 tokens for Llama-3.1-8B) against EAGLE-3, EAGLE-1 and n-gram drafting inside vLLM and SGLang, with GPU energy per token read from the hardware energy counter. At batch size 1 on an RTX 5090, the draft-model configuration raises throughput by 60-79% and roughly halves energy per token compared with non-speculative decoding; a well-configured EAGLE-3 is 8-14% faster, with energy per token within about 10% either way. This is not a new algorithm: the contribution is the measurement protocol and results. See the README for scope and limitations.

title: Dimensional Geometry Adaptive Quantum Computing
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of dimensionality-aware quantum computing, specifically exploring the concept of a novel approach that leverages quantum entanglement to expand computational space beyond the limitations of classical physics. We introduce a new method for manipulating quantum states through a geometric transformation, enabling calculations in higher dimensions without the need for traditional positional operations. The core mechanism centers around establishing a quantum entanglement network to directly map quantum states to higher-dimensional spaces, exploiting the correlated nature of entanglement to perform computations. The study aims to demonstrate the feasibility of this approach, highlighting its potential to address complex problems currently intractable for classical computers. The proposed method promises a paradigm shift in quantum algorithm design and offers a pathway to fundamentally expand the capabilities of quantum computation.

title: 自适应几何拓扑模型
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to quantum computing involving the design of an adaptive geometric topology model. Traditional parameter adjustments in quantum computing often rely on manual tuning, lacking the inherent topological structure that can significantly enhance system performance. We propose a system that automatically adjusts the geometric structure of quantum systems based on input data, optimizing quantum computation efficiency. The core mechanism utilizes the principles of geometric topology to dynamically modify the system's configuration. This adaptive approach represents a significant advancement over existing techniques, offering a potential pathway toward more efficient and robust quantum algorithms. The paper details the model's architecture, explains the underlying mathematical principles, and provides preliminary results demonstrating its effectiveness.

title: Based on Formal Languages for Automated Theorem Proving in Program Verification
abstract: This paper explores the application of formal languages and automated theorem proving techniques to achieve automated program verification. The core concept involves representing programs within formal languages, leveraging the inherent deductive capabilities of these languages, and integrating automated theorem provers to generate proofs of program correctness. This approach contrasts with traditional, largely manual, program verification methods by introducing an automated process. The primary focus is on demonstrating the feasibility and potential benefits of this combined methodology, with a particular emphasis on reducing the effort and potential errors associated with manual verification. The techniques detailed herein aim to establish a foundation for more robust and scalable program verification systems. The paper outlines key challenges and future research directions within this domain.

title: Adaptive Quantum Topology Optimization
abstract: Quantum topology optimization (QTO) is a novel approach to designing and optimizing quantum systems by leveraging the inherent topology of quantum systems to guide parameter adjustments. This paper explores the development of a quantum optimization algorithm, termed "Adaptive Quantum Topology Optimization" (AQTO), that dynamically adapts to the system's topology, enabling efficient parameter tuning and improved results. We introduce a novel 'dynamic topology map' that iteratively refines the system's topology based on the optimization process, ensuring optimal performance. The benefits of this algorithm, including enhanced flexibility, robustness, and the potential for discovering novel solutions, are discussed. The paper concludes with a detailed explanation of the AQTO algorithm, its mathematical formulation, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating its effectiveness.

title: Quantum Entanglement Topological Geometry Modeling with Adaptive Parameter Tuning
abstract: Quantum entanglement offers a fundamentally different approach to geometric modeling compared to traditional methods. This paper explores the utilization of quantum entanglement to automatically adjust geometric modeling parameters, resulting in enhanced modeling precision. We propose a novel method centered around leveraging the unique properties of entangled quantum states to dynamically modify the geometry of a defined space. This approach avoids the need for manual parameter tuning, offering a potentially more efficient and accurate modeling process. The core mechanism involves an entanglement-based algorithm that iteratively refines the geometric configuration based on the inherent correlations within the entangled system. We present a preliminary implementation demonstrating this adaptive parameter adjustment process, showcasing improved accuracy in a specific geometric model. The research aims to advance the field of geometric modeling by integrating quantum entanglement into a sophisticated optimization technique.

title: ##基于多智能体强化学习的物理定律发现
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to discovering and validating fundamental physical laws using Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL). The core idea is to leverage the interactions and competition among multiple agents within a simulated physical environment to autonomously identify and verify potential laws governing the system. Each agent is trained using a reinforcement learning algorithm, receiving rewards for behaviors that align with observed physical patterns. This approach offers a dynamic and automated method for uncovering hidden relationships and constraints, potentially leading to the discovery of new physical laws or the refinement of existing ones. The presented framework emphasizes exploration and utilizes agent interactions to drive the learning process. This research addresses the limitations of traditional physics discovery methods by introducing a system capable of adapting to complex environments and identifying patterns that might be missed by human observation. The key innovations lie in the application of MARL to this domain and the design of a reward structure that effectively guides agents toward discovering physical laws. ---

title: Quantum Entanglement Dynamics: A Dynamic Computational Framework
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic computational framework for quantum entanglement, leveraging adaptive spin parameters to enable dynamic entanglement changes and high-precision calculations. Traditional approaches to quantum entanglement computation rely on static parameter settings, while our framework utilizes adaptive learning algorithms and self-adjusting entanglement degree adjustment mechanisms to achieve dynamic entanglement evolution. The core mechanism involves dynamically modifying the spin state of entangled particles, offering a significant advancement in the capabilities of quantum computation. This work explores the potential of this approach to overcome limitations inherent in conventional methods and address fundamental challenges in the field.

title: 基于量子态的自适应扰动算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-adaptive perturbation algorithm based on quantum state representation. Traditional perturbation methods often rely on manual parameter tuning, limiting their adaptability. This work proposes a quantum state-driven approach that automatically adjusts perturbation parameters based on the algorithm's output, resulting in enhanced perturbation effectiveness. We explore the application of quantum state analysis to achieve this adaptive control. The core mechanism involves encoding the input data into a quantum state and leveraging this state to dynamically adjust the perturbation parameters, providing a more robust and efficient approach to perturbing systems. The proposed algorithm demonstrates improved performance across a range of perturbation tasks, showcasing the potential of quantum state representation for adaptive control.

title: Quantum-Inspired Optimization of Large-Scale Distributed Algorithms
abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum-inspired optimization techniques to accelerate the convergence of large-scale distributed algorithms. Traditional distributed algorithm design often relies on classical optimization methods, which can struggle with the complexity and scale inherent in these systems. We propose a novel approach that borrows concepts from quantum mechanics, specifically amplitude amplification and interference, to guide the search for optimal solutions. The core idea is to utilize superposition and interference effects to explore a broader solution space more efficiently than conventional methods. We formulate a generalized framework for integrating these techniques, focusing on the iterative refinement of algorithm parameters. Preliminary analysis and theoretical considerations suggest that this approach holds promise for significant performance improvements in areas such as sensor network routing, distributed machine learning, and consensus protocols. This research aims to bridge the gap between quantum computing concepts and classical distributed systems, offering a potentially transformative method for optimizing algorithm performance.

title: Black-shanked Douc Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Douc-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization (DIMHO)," inspired by the foraging behavior of the Black-shanked Douc, a primate known for its complex and efficient search strategies. The algorithm incorporates key aspects of the Douc's movement patterns – including adaptive step sizes, clustered exploration, and a dynamic adjustment of search parameters – into its core optimization process. DIMHO leverages a population-based approach combined with a novel adaptive parameter control mechanism. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time. Specifically, we explore the algorithm's performance on the Rastrigin, Sphere, and Powell test functions. The key contribution of this work lies in the unique integration of behavioral characteristics of a specific animal into a metaheuristic framework, offering a potentially valuable tool for tackling complex and challenging optimization problems. The algorithm's performance is compared with established metaheuristic methods such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The results indicate that DIMHO exhibits competitive performance, particularly in scenarios requiring adaptive exploration and exploitation strategies.

title: Beisa: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Behavior of Beisa Whistling Ducks
abstract: This paper presents Beisa, a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the unique whistling behavior of Beisa whistling ducks. The algorithm leverages the duck's ability to precisely mimic sounds and their intricate territorial defense strategies to develop a novel search process. Beisa combines elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) with a dynamic adaptation mechanism based on frequency modulation and amplitude variation, mimicking the duck's vocalizations. The algorithm's core features include a dynamic population size, adaptive inertia weight, and a novel convergence criterion. Theoretical analysis demonstrates the algorithm's potential for efficient exploration and exploitation within complex search spaces. Performance evaluations on a range of benchmark functions reveal that Beisa consistently outperforms several established metaheuristic algorithms, including PSO, ABC, and Genetic Algorithm (GA), particularly in problems with high dimensionality and complex landscapes. The algorithm's adaptive nature and the inspiration from a natural phenomenon contribute to its robustness and effectiveness. Future research will focus on incorporating the algorithm into real-world applications and further refining its parameters for optimal performance.
