title: Quantum-Inspired Anomaly Detection in Time Series Data
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to anomaly detection in time series data inspired by quantum mechanics, specifically quantum superposition and interference. Traditional anomaly detection methods often struggle with subtle deviations that may be masked within noisy data or require significant domain expertise to identify. Our method leverages the inherent properties of quantum states to represent time series data, enabling the generation of interference patterns that can amplify weak anomalies. We formulate the detection process as a measurement problem within a quantum framework, where the act of measurement itself can accentuate deviations from the expected quantum state. The core idea is to represent the time series as a superposition of possible states, and then observe the interference patterns resulting from this superposition. Anomalous events cause a shift in the interference pattern, which can be detected with higher sensitivity than traditional statistical methods. This approach offers the potential to significantly improve anomaly detection performance, particularly in scenarios with complex, high-dimensional time series data. The theoretical framework is presented, followed by a discussion of the key mathematical concepts and operational considerations. The paper concludes with a summary of the proposed method and its potential future directions.

title: Adaptive Quantum Control Theory
abstract: This paper introduces Adaptive Quantum Control Theory (AQCT), a novel framework designed to address the challenges inherent in controlling quantum systems. Traditional quantum control methods often rely on precise, pre-determined control signals, which can be highly sensitive to system imperfections and environmental noise. AQCT leverages the principles of reinforcement learning and quantum control theory to create a controller capable of dynamically adapting its control strategy based on the real-time state of the quantum system. The core mechanism involves designing a controller that learns and optimizes control policies through iterative interaction with the system, effectively mitigating the impact of uncertainties. This approach promises improved control performance, robustness, and scalability for a wide range of quantum systems. The theoretical framework presented here lays a foundation for future research and development in adaptive quantum control.

title: Quantum Entanglement Encoding-Based Non-Classical Communication Protocol
abstract: This paper proposes a novel communication protocol leveraging multi-particle entanglement for non-classical information transmission. The core of the protocol resides in a carefully designed encoding scheme utilizing multi-variable entangled states to mitigate the impact of quantum decoherence and achieve information transfer rates exceeding the classical channel capacity. We introduce a multi-variable entangled state based error correction coding mechanism, combined with quantum decoherence theory, providing a scalable error correction strategy. The protocol focuses on precise control of entangled state utilization and minimizing errors in non-classical communication, offering a potentially scalable solution. The key mathematical formulation explores the encoding process, error detection, and correction stages, highlighting the role of entangled correlations in recovering the transmitted information. This work contributes to the advancement of quantum communication by providing a robust and scalable approach to non-classical information transfer. ---

title: ## Bala Tube-nosed Bat-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the Bala Tube-nosed Bat (BTNB) algorithm, inspired by the foraging behavior of the Bala tube-nosed bat (Macronycteris perspiculus). These bats exhibit a unique and highly efficient foraging strategy characterized by a complex movement pattern involving both hovering and directed flight. The BTNB algorithm leverages these behavioral traits to create a robust and adaptive search process. The core of the algorithm involves a population of bats, each represented by a position vector (xi, yi) in a two-dimensional space. The movement of each bat is governed by a dynamic adjustment of its velocity vector (vix, viy) influenced by its position, the global best position, and a random component. The algorithm utilizes a 'leader-follower' mechanism, mimicking the bats' hierarchical structure, where the best-positioned bats influence the movement of others. The convergence rate and performance of the BTNB algorithm are evaluated through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and potential for tackling complex, non-linear optimization challenges. The algorithm's key parameters – inertia weight (ω), cognitive coefficient (c1), and social coefficient (c2) – are tuned to optimize performance across diverse problem landscapes. The results show that the BTNB algorithm consistently outperforms traditional metaheuristic methods like the Genetic Algorithm and Particle Swarm Optimization in terms of solution quality and convergence speed.

title: Quantum Information & Non-Linear Logic Systems: A Fusion Approach
abstract: Quantum information theory holds immense promise for revolutionizing computation, and the development of Non-Linear Logic Systems (NLSS) offers a compelling avenue for exploring novel computational paradigms. This paper delves into the integration of quantum information principles with NLSS, proposing a framework for constructing a quantum computing architecture that leverages the system's inherent non-linear properties. We explore the potential for enhanced data compression and encoding through this fusion, aiming to improve the efficiency of quantum computation. This work presents a detailed investigation of the design and implementation of a quantum computing model based on NLSS, focusing on the synergistic effects of its non-linear logic and quantum processing capabilities.

title: Title: Temporal Dynamics in Machine Learning Regularization (TDMR)
abstract: Temporal Dynamics in Machine Learning Regularization (TDMR) proposes a novel approach to machine learning model regularization that dynamically adjusts regularization parameters based on the temporal evolution of the data. This addresses the issue of concept drift, a significant challenge in many real-world applications, by proactively mitigating it through adaptive parameter adjustments. The research introduces a recurrent neural network (RNN) to analyze data trends, enabling the model to adjust regularization strength as the data shifts, thereby improving robustness and generalization. This paper will detail the methodology, experimental results, and insights gained, demonstrating the effectiveness of TDMR in mitigating concept drift.

title: ## The Pacific Cod Inspired Adaptive Search Algorithm (PACISA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Pacific Cod Inspired Adaptive Search Algorithm (PACISA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the migratory patterns and feeding strategies of Pacific Cod. PACISA leverages the cod's ability to dynamically adjust its search range based on environmental cues and prey availability, mirroring the concept of adaptive exploration and exploitation. The algorithm employs a population-based approach, utilizing a 'school' of cod agents, each with individual search vectors. These agents iteratively adjust their positions based on a combination of global best position, local best position, and a dynamically adjusted adaptive parameter influenced by the perceived density of 'prey' (potential solutions) in the search space. The algorithm's core innovation lies in its adaptive parameter, which is not fixed but changes over time, reflecting the cod's shifting behavior in response to changing conditions. This paper details the algorithm's design, outlining its key components and the rationale behind their selection, drawing parallels to the observed behaviors of Pacific Cod.

title: ## Arizona Myotis: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of the Arizona Myotis Bat
abstract: This paper introduces Arizona Myotis (AZM), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging strategies employed by the Arizona Myotis bat. AZM leverages the bat's echolocation and dynamic movement patterns to navigate complex search spaces and converge towards optimal solutions. The algorithm utilizes a modified version of the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) framework, incorporating elements of bat foraging behavior including a dynamic exploration phase, a target-seeking mechanism, and a polarization strategy. We present the mathematical formulation of AZM, detailing the key parameters and equations governing its operation. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark test functions, demonstrating its effectiveness and competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms. We demonstrate AZM's adaptability and potential for application in various optimization problems, particularly those exhibiting complex, non-linear landscapes. The core concepts and mathematical representation of AZM are presented in detail, offering a robust and efficient approach to global optimization.

title: ## Bioluminescent Navigation Algorithm (BNA): A Metaheuristic Optimization Inspired by Lanternfish
abstract: This paper introduces the Bioluminescent Navigation Algorithm (BNA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the unique navigation behavior of lanternfish ( *Myctophidae*). Lanternfish utilize bioluminescence to create a dynamic, self-organizing, and highly efficient swarm for schooling and foraging. BNA leverages these principles – particularly the concept of 'leading light' and 'following light' – to facilitate exploration and exploitation in optimization problems. The algorithm employs a population-based approach, simulating the movement of lanternfish within a defined search space. Key components include a 'leading fish' selection mechanism, a 'following fish' adaptation strategy, and a dynamic weighting scheme for guiding the search towards promising regions. The algorithm's performance is evaluated theoretically, demonstrating its potential for navigating complex, multi-dimensional search landscapes. Future research will focus on implementing BNA in various optimization applications and validating its effectiveness through computational experiments.

title: Quantum Entanglement and Higher-Dimensional Spacetime Geometry
abstract: Quantum entanglement presents a fundamentally challenging concept for classical physics, offering a potential pathway to manipulating space-time geometry. This paper explores the theoretical implications of leveraging quantum entanglement to "deconstruct" certain geometric properties within higher-dimensional spaces, ultimately leading to a novel quantum computing paradigm suitable for large-scale computations. We propose a framework based on quantum geometry, employing entanglement to establish an abstract model, and subsequently, applying this model to optimize quantum computation's performance. The core claim is that this approach provides a unique perspective on harnessing entanglement to reshape the geometry of higher-dimensional spaces, offering a potential breakthrough in quantum computing.

title: Title: Non-Local Quantum State Analysis for Dynamical Systems with Non-Linearity
abstract: Quantum state analysis is a fundamental tool in understanding complex dynamical systems, particularly those exhibiting non-linear behavior. Traditional approaches often struggle with high-dimensional systems due to computational complexity and the inherent difficulty in capturing complex correlations. This paper introduces a novel quantum algorithm, "Non-Local Quantum State Analysis," designed to address these challenges by leveraging quantum entanglement to explore the relationship between states across multiple dimensions, uncovering hidden patterns and dynamics. The core mechanism centers around creating entangled states that represent correlated variables, enabling the algorithm to simultaneously analyze the system's evolution across various dimensions and identify emergent behaviors. We present a preliminary demonstration of this algorithm, focusing on a simplified example of a non-linear dynamical system, illustrating its potential for revealing intricate correlations and dynamics that are often missed by classical methods. The algorithm's inherent advantages lie in its ability to directly exploit quantum correlations, offering a fundamentally different perspective on system analysis.

title: Formal Modeling of Black-Box Systems using Counterfactual Explanations
abstract: Black-box systems, prevalent across numerous domains, pose a significant challenge to understanding and trust. Traditional methods of analysis, such as behavioral testing and simulation, often fall short due to the inherent opacity and complexity of these systems. This paper introduces a novel approach to formally modeling black-box systems by leveraging counterfactual explanations. We propose a framework that generates "what if" scenarios – counterfactual examples – designed to elicit alternative system behaviors. These counterfactual examples are then used to construct a formal model, represented as a set of logical rules, that captures the system's conditional behavior. The resulting model provides a verifiable and interpretable representation, enhancing understanding and potentially facilitating improved system design and operation. The core contribution lies in the formalization of black-box system behavior through counterfactual reasoning, offering a practical tool for dealing with systems where transparency is limited.

title: Self-Supervised Learning for Graph Embedding with Relational Reasoning
abstract: Graph embedding techniques have become increasingly prevalent in various domains, including social network analysis, knowledge graph reasoning, and drug discovery. However, many existing methods primarily focus on learning node representations based on node features or immediate neighborhood structures, often failing to effectively capture intricate relationships and dependencies within graphs. This paper proposes a novel self-supervised learning framework for graph embedding that explicitly incorporates relational reasoning. The core idea is to train node embeddings by predicting missing edges within the graph, leveraging the relational context surrounding each node. This approach allows nodes to learn richer and more informative representations that reflect the underlying graph structure and its associated relationships. We formulate the problem as a masked edge prediction task, where nodes are tasked with inferring the presence or absence of edges based on their connected nodes and the graph's relational structure. The learned embeddings are then used for downstream tasks such as node classification and link prediction. Experimental results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach compared to state-of-the-art graph embedding methods, highlighting its ability to learn more robust and accurate representations.

title: ## Sardine Atlantic: A Bio-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Global Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces "Sardine Atlantic," a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of Atlantic sardines. These fish exhibit a remarkable ability to navigate vast oceanic spaces, efficiently locating food resources while avoiding predators. Sardine Atlantic leverages this behavior through a dynamic, decentralized exploration strategy, combined with a hierarchical aggregation mechanism. The algorithm utilizes a population of "sardines" represented as vectors in a search space, with each sardine possessing a position, speed, and direction. A "schooling" concept is introduced, where sardines dynamically adjust their positions based on the collective movement of their neighbors, mimicking the flocking behavior of sardines. Furthermore, a hierarchical aggregation process is employed to guide the search towards promising regions of the solution space. The algorithm's parameters are adjusted based on the observed movement patterns of the sardines, aiming to emulate the adaptive strategies utilized by these fish. This paper details the algorithm's design, mathematical formulation, and presents a conceptual overview of its operational principles.

title: ##基于量子纠错码的分布式计算架构
abstract: This paper proposes a novel distributed computing architecture leveraging quantum error-correcting codes for robust and scalable quantum computation. The core idea is to utilize the inherent error correction capabilities of these codes within a distributed setting, mitigating the challenges associated with maintaining qubit coherence over long distances and facilitating large-scale quantum processing. We detail a framework where multiple quantum processors, interconnected via quantum channels, employ a specific quantum error-correcting code to encode and decode quantum information. This approach directly addresses the key limitations of current quantum computing architectures, offering a pathway towards achieving fault-tolerant quantum computation. The architecture is designed to enhance resilience against noise and errors, a critical factor for practical quantum computation. The theoretical framework presented outlines the key components and operational principles, focusing on the encoding and decoding process using a chosen quantum error-correcting code. We provide a mathematical analysis of the system, detailing the redundancy introduced by the code and the impact on computational complexity. The architecture's potential for scaling to larger quantum systems and its implications for various quantum algorithms are discussed. This work represents a significant step towards realizing the full potential of distributed quantum computing.

title: Quantum Entanglement Generator-Driven Distributed Reasoning
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to distributed reasoning leveraging quantum entanglement generators. The core concept involves constructing a network of nodes, each equipped with an entanglement generator producing specific entangled states. Information and computations are transmitted and processed via quantum entanglement, eliminating the need for classical communication. The system's efficiency and reach are determined by the types and generation rates of entangled states. We demonstrate that this architecture offers a significant departure from traditional distributed computing paradigms, potentially overcoming inherent bottlenecks associated with classical communication overhead. The theoretical framework outlines the key components and operational principles, highlighting the potential for scalable and high-performance distributed reasoning tasks. This approach aims to unlock new computational possibilities by harnessing the unique properties of quantum entanglement. The primary mathematical model presented focuses on entanglement fidelity, generation rates, and the information transfer efficiency within the network.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Collaborative Learning
abstract: This paper proposes a novel framework for neuro-symbolic collaborative learning, aiming to leverage the strengths of both deep learning and neuro-symbolic reasoning. The core idea is to establish a synergistic interaction between a deep neural network (DNN) and a neuro-symbolic engine, enabling more efficient and robust learning. The DNN is responsible for perceptual data processing and generating probabilistic symbolic representations, while the neuro-symbolic engine performs logical inference on these representations, producing new symbolic representations and providing feedback to the DNN for refinement. The learning process is optimized through reinforcement learning or genetic algorithms, focusing on the collaborative interplay between these two components. This approach addresses the limitations of existing methods that often treat deep learning and neuro-symbolic approaches as independent, offering a dynamic and iterative learning system. The key contributions lie in the cyclical feedback loop and the integrated optimization strategy, leading to a more powerful learning paradigm.

title: Title: Dynamically Generated Constraint Networks for Adaptive Robotics
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to adaptive robotics, leveraging dynamically generated constraint networks to enhance task planning and robot behavior. Traditional robotic planning relies heavily on pre-defined constraints, often limiting the robot's flexibility and hindering its ability to handle unforeseen circumstances. We introduce a system that automatically constructs constraint networks tailored to the robot's specific dynamics and the environment, thereby enabling more robust and adaptable robot control. The core mechanism centers around a learned model of the robot's dynamics, which is then used to generate constraint networks that adapt in real-time. This approach significantly improves the robot's ability to navigate complex environments and execute tasks safely and efficiently. The system is evaluated through simulations, demonstrating substantial improvements in task completion accuracy and robustness compared to traditional constraint-based methods.

title: Title: Non-Local Quantum State Synchronization & Correlation
abstract: Quantum state synchronization and correlation are fundamental challenges in quantum information theory, crucial for distributed quantum computation and quantum key distribution. Current approaches often rely on classical communication, which introduces latency and limits scalability. This paper explores a novel approach to synchronize and correlate quantum states across spatially separated locations using a 'Quantum Entanglement Network' architecture. We detail the design principles, mathematical formulations, and potential implementation of this method, highlighting its potential to overcome limitations inherent in existing quantum communication paradigms. The core claim centers on establishing a robust and efficient method for synchronizing and correlating quantum states, paving the way for distributed quantum computation.

title: Information-Theoretic Entropy Encoding of Time Series Data
abstract: This paper investigates the application of information-theoretic entropy coding techniques to the compression of time series data. The core claim is that time series data can be compressed to its theoretical information limit, leading to unprecedented compression ratios. The proposed method analyzes the statistical properties of the time series, employing an optimal entropy coder – specifically Huffman coding and arithmetic coding – to represent the data efficiently. We demonstrate that this approach, grounded in fundamental information theory principles, offers a fundamentally different and potentially superior compression strategy compared to conventional time series compression algorithms, unlocking new possibilities for data storage and transmission. The analysis focuses on the theoretical limits of compression and the practical considerations of implementing entropy coding for dynamic time series.

title: Quantum Entanglement Information Decoding: A Self-Adaptive Cryptographic Approach
abstract: Quantum entanglement offers a fundamentally new paradigm for secure communication, potentially exceeding the capabilities of classical cryptography. This paper explores the application of quantum entanglement to create a self-adaptive encryption scheme. We propose a system where the encryption process dynamically adjusts to subtle changes in a sender's or receiver's quantum state, thereby enhancing security against various attacks. The core mechanism centers around a "quantum state sensitivity" mechanism, which modulates the entanglement strength to maintain the integrity of the key. This innovative approach leverages the unique properties of quantum entanglement to create a resilient and adaptable encryption protocol. The potential benefits of this design include increased resistance to known cryptanalytic attacks, a shift towards a more robust security paradigm, and the exploration of novel cryptographic techniques.

Our model leverages the inherent chaotic dynamics of self-organization to dynamically adjust the computation domain, enabling efficient resource utilization and enhanced performance. The core mechanism involves the continuous evolution of the computation field, driven by a feedback loop that optimizes for accuracy and speed. We demonstrate the model's effectiveness through theoretical analysis and preliminary simulations, highlighting its potential to revolutionize quantum computation.

title: Dynamic Topology-Based Adaptive Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel adaptive optimization algorithm based on dynamic topology. Traditional optimization methods rely on static target functions, limiting their flexibility and adaptability. This work proposes a dynamic topology approach where the optimization objective is dynamically adjusted based on input data. The algorithm iteratively refines the optimization target function to improve performance and robustness. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of rigorous experiments across multiple benchmark datasets. The core mechanism involves constructing a dynamic topology structure that adapts to the input data, allowing for more intelligent and efficient optimization.

title: An Improved Honey Badger Algorithm Based on Urban Traffic-Inspired Strategies for Global Optimization and Financial Corporate Bankruptcy Forecasting
abstract: To address the limitations of the original Honey Badger Algorithm (HBA), including premature convergence, limited search directionality, and insufficient local escape capability in high-dimensional complex optimization problems, this paper proposes an improved Honey Badger Algorithm based on a traffic-driven strategy, namely the Traffic-driven Covariance Honey Badger Algorithm (TCHBA). The proposed algorithm introduces three synergistic evolutionary mechanisms. First, Elite Covariance Rotation Guidance learns correlated search directions from the current elite subset and injects a truncated covariance-based step into the HBA update. Second, Urban Traffic-Inspired Search uses population density and an iteration-dependent signal to regulate attraction and diversion. Third, Stagnation-Aware Lens Opposition Mutation is activated after unsuccessful updates and combines lens opposition with a heavy-tailed Cauchy perturbation to restore search mobility. Extensive experiments are conducted on the CEC2017 (100-dimensional) and CEC2022 (10- and 20-dimensional) benchmark suites. The results demonstrate that TCHBA significantly outperforms nine state-of-the-art optimization algorithms, including VPPSO, EGWO, GJO, RIME, ALA, HBO, MO, PWO, and the original HBA, in terms of solution accuracy, convergence speed, and statistical robustness. Furthermore, TCHBA is applied to the problem of Taiwanese enterprise bankruptcy prediction, a representative financial risk classification task. By optimizing the key parameters of the K-nearest neighbors (KNN) classifier, a TCHBA-KNN prediction model is constructed. Experimental results on real-world datasets show that the proposed model achieves superior performance in terms of accuracy, Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC), recall, and F1-score, thereby validating the effectiveness and practical potential of the proposed algorithm for real-world engineering and financial decision-making problems.

title: Context Window Failures in Relational Foundation Models
abstract: Recent Relational Deep Learning architectures have been proposed as foundation models for multi-table relational data, yet they impose constrained neighborhood budgets that force row truncation when an entity has many related records. We introduce Animus, a synthetic financial dataset in which predicting customer income requires aggregating up to tens of thousands of transactions. On the raw representation, three recently proposed models (RT, Griffin, RelGT) achieve $R^2 \le 0.18$; a single, routine, temporal pre-aggregation step recovers $R^2$ up to $0.65$. This questions whether current relational foundation models are ready for high-cardinality real-world data.

title: Generative artificial intelligence for reliable mechanistic reasoning for corrosion
abstract: Corrosion accounts for approximately 4% of global GDP, and reliable prediction is essential for timely mitigation. Machine learning effectively predicts corrosion rates from composition, microstructure, and environmental variables, but cannot explain the underlying mechanisms. A reliable approach in safety-critical materials engineering requires not only accurate retrieval but also mechanistically defensible reasoning, a capability that existing factuality metrics cannot assess. This work presents a domain-adapted retrieval-augmented generation framework for corrosion knowledge synthesis, demonstrated on magnesium alloy corrosion. Three open-weight language models (Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen-2.5-7B, Mistral-7B) are fine-tuned on 3,309 expert-verified question-answer pairs from 840 peer-reviewed papers and integrated with a hybrid dense-lexical retrieval pipeline. Retrieval augmentation produces Token F1 gains of 143-194%, with system faithfulness of 0.964 and context recall of 0.988. Blind external validation on newly published literature and in-house electrochemical data confirms trend-level generalisation. Reason Map, a proposition-graph framework, is further introduced; it independently constructs directed evidence graphs from generated answers and retrieved literature, enabling systematic detection of causal direction inversions and unsupported inferential leaps that flat factuality metrics cannot expose. The modular architecture can be applied across domains, offering a generalizable blueprint for trustworthy AI-assisted knowledge synthesis to circumvent corrosion, which can also be applied to other engineering domains.

title: An Agentic Retrobiosynthesis Framework with Learned Frontier Selection
abstract: Large language models are increasingly used as agents for multistep retrosynthesis, raising the question of how much their search policy contributes independently of the underlying reaction model. We investigate this question in a biological setting through rule-based retrobiosynthesis: a deterministic biochemical engine generates the same validated transitions for every method, searching for routes that terminate in metabolites available to an \emph{Escherichia coli} chassis, while the policy only selects which frontier molecule to expand next. Prompted and LoRA-tuned Qwen2.5-7B policies use a strict choice-only interface. The fine-tuned policy reaches $65\pm1$\% solve rate at 10 expansions on LASER versus 59\% for MCTS, and at 200 expansions reaches $78\pm1$\% versus 75\% on LASER, $88\pm3$\% versus 80\% on the RetroPath RL Golden benchmark, and $63\pm2$\% versus 45\% on the BioNavi-NP benchmark. Fine-tuning also consistently outperforms direct prompting. These results show that route-supervised frontier selection can improve budgeted search without altering biochemical generation, although performance remains dependent on frontier construction and reaction ranking.

title: FlowVVTON: Flow-Guided Mask-Free Video Virtual Try-On
abstract: Video virtual try-on aims to transfer a target garment onto a moving person across video frames. Current methods rely on human parsing masks or pose keypoints that frequently fail under large motions and occlusions, causing boundary artifacts and temporal inconsistency. A further limitation is that most approaches rely solely on attention mechanisms for temporal modeling, providing no explicit motion supervision. We propose FlowVVTON, a mask-free framework that eliminates parsing mask dependency entirely. Optical flow is used solely as a training-time supervision signal: a flow-warped latent loss, applied across all layers of the generation model, enforces multi-scale temporal consistency by aligning adjacent-frame features under explicit physical motion constraints. A two-stage training strategy establishes mask-free spatial alignment before introducing flow-guided temporal supervision. Experiments on TikTokDress show that FlowVVTON outperforms baselines by substantial margins, particularly in temporal consistency (5.7$\times$ VFID-R improvement over SwiftTry), while requiring no segmentation masks, pose keypoints, or region annotations at any stage.

title: Indirect stabilization of N -level quantum systems
abstract: We study the stabilizability of a N -level quantum systems using an indirect control ar- chitecture mediated by a noisy ancilla. After outlining the general theoretical framework for arbitrary N , we focus on the two-level case (N = 2), for which we derive a complete set of necessary and sufficient conditions for asymptotic stability. Finally, we illustrate the analyti- cal results with a simple numerical example on a two-spin system, showing convergence to a Bell state for a set of random initial conditions.

title: Estrategias didácticas y competencias pedagógicas en la enseñanza de robótica infantil: estudio diagnóstico
abstract: La educación inicial (edades comprendidas entre 0-6 años) enfrenta un reto importante: integrar la robótica educativa garantizando aprendizajes significativos a través de la mediación pedagógica. Este estudio examina de qué manera las estrategias didácticas y competencias pedagógicas actúan como mediadores en la enseñanza de la robótica dentro de marcos constructivistas. Se aplicó una encuesta diagnóstica de tipo descriptiva a 11 educadores de educación inicial en la Unidad Educativa Colegio Privado Los Cedros, Trujillo, Venezuela, utilizando un instrumento validado de 16 ítems, organizados en seis dimensiones: planificación didáctica, estrategias metodológicas, gestión de recursos, prácticas de evaluación, formación docente e intencionalidad pedagógica. El análisis de datos reveló que el 64% de los docentes emplean estrategias consolidadas en intencionalidad pedagógica, sin embargo, apenas un 36% logra gestionar adecuadamente los recursos físicos. Los docentes con competencias tecnológico-pedagógicas avanzadas diseñan experiencias de aprendizaje significativamente más estructuradas (p < 0,05). Llama la atención que el 91% reconoce el valor de la robótica, pero la práctica choca contra la falta de infraestructura. A partir de estos datos, sostenemos que el artefacto por sí solo no educa; la verdadera transformación sociocognitiva depende del diseño de las estrategias mediadoras de la docente. Esta investigación proporciona orientación fundamentada en evidencia para iniciativas de desarrollo profesional que contribuye a la intersección poco estudiada entre tecnología educativa, pedagogía constructivista y resultados de aprendizaje en educación temprana.

title: A Dataset of Historical‑Character Portrayals Based on Event‑Level Sentiment Annotations
abstract: This dataset supports the research on an automated framework for historical‑figure profiling. It records the data and results generated at each stage of the experiment. It comprises four parts: Label Classification.xlsx, covering the label classification of historical‑figure events; Categorisation and Sentiment Polarity.xlsx, covering event categorisation and the associated sentiment polarity; Sentiment Consistency.xlsx, covering the consistency between event sentiment and evaluative sentiment; and Sentiment Sequences.xlsx, covering the temporal sentiment sequences of historical‑figure events.

title: What a Multi-Model Adjudication Machine Converges On: APEX's Methods and an Honest Convergence Record
abstract: APEX generates cross-domain hypotheses and adjudicates each with several independently calibrated language models from distinct families; a claim is 'confirmed' only when ≥2 families independently judge the external literature to strongly support it, with zero refutations. Seven met that bar. The honest finding is not 'seven discoveries.' Five of the seven are the same well-established idea — a measurement/operationalization framework has blind spots fixed by its own constraints (the theory-ladenness of observation; operationalism's critique; Goodhart's Law) — and the other two are also nameable as prior art. The result is therefore a statement about the machine: given open rein and a multi-family gate, it repeatedly rediscovers one established cluster rather than finding something new. One claim that first read as 'possibly novel' was named, in one shot, as Goodhart's Law. This deposit releases the reusable adjudication protocol (refute-gate calibration, family-level confirmation, self-echo exclusion, two-naming novelty check) and the open records so others can re-adjudicate with their own witnesses. 'Confirmed' means replicated, not discovered; none of the seven is novel.

title: 基于自适应拓扑结构的量子态计算框架
abstract: Quantum state computation is a rapidly advancing field with significant potential for revolutionizing various scientific and technological applications. Traditional methods often struggle to effectively handle the complexities inherent in quantum states, particularly when dealing with intricate geometric structures. This paper proposes a novel quantum state calculation framework, leveraging the unique properties of self-adjoint geometry to precisely model and optimize quantum states. We introduce a dynamic, adaptive topology structure that allows for the exploration of novel quantum states and efficient manipulation of existing ones. The framework emphasizes the use of geometric transformations to reveal hidden quantum information, offering a significant improvement over existing techniques in terms of accuracy, speed, and adaptability. We present a detailed theoretical analysis of the framework, demonstrating its efficacy through simulations and preliminary results. The core mechanism involves constructing and manipulating a self-adjoint topology that encodes the quantum state, enabling precise calculations and optimization. This work addresses a long-standing challenge in quantum state computation, paving the way for more advanced quantum algorithms and a deeper understanding of quantum mechanics.

title: ##拓扑混沌量子态的自适应几何优化
abstract: This paper investigates the integration of quantum state topology optimization with the principles of chaotic dynamics, aiming to achieve precise control over quantum states and enhance the stability of quantum computation. We propose a novel optimization algorithm that dynamically adjusts quantum potential fields, guided by the inherent self-organization of chaotic systems. The core mechanism centers around constructing a geometric framework that allows for 'quantum jumps' – a departure from traditional deterministic quantum evolution – potentially leading to significant improvements in quantum performance. The study explores how this combined approach can mitigate inherent uncertainties in quantum systems and unlock new avenues for quantum algorithm design. We present a preliminary design and analysis of this framework, highlighting its potential impact on quantum state manipulation and computational efficiency.

title: Emergent Cognitive Engine Based on Biological Neural Networks
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to cognitive engine design by leveraging the principles of biological neural networks. The core idea is to construct a computational system capable of exhibiting emergent cognitive abilities through the emulation of self-organization and synaptic plasticity found in the brain. Specifically, we utilize Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) combined with plasticity mechanisms like long-term potentiation (LTP) and self-organizing learning algorithms. This architecture aims to bypass the limitations of traditional cognitive computing, which often relies on pre-programmed rules and explicit knowledge representation. The system's adaptive nature, stemming from its inherent ability to learn and reorganize itself, offers a potentially more robust and flexible solution for cognitive tasks. The research investigates the feasibility and effectiveness of this approach, focusing on the emergent properties arising from the network's dynamics. We explore the influence of parameters within the SNN model and the impact of different self-organization strategies on the overall cognitive performance. Ultimately, this work contributes to a deeper understanding of how biological neural networks generate intelligence and provides a framework for developing adaptive and intelligent systems.

title: Quantum Entangled Matrix Nonlinear Computation
abstract: Quantum Entangled Matrix Nonlinear Computation is a novel approach to solving linear algebra problems by leveraging quantum entanglement to efficiently compute non-linear operations. This paper explores the design of a quantum computing method utilizing entangled matrices to accelerate linear algebra computations, ultimately aiming to expand the capabilities of quantum computation. The core mechanism centers around harnessing the unique properties of quantum entanglement to enable a fundamentally faster and more scalable approach to solving linear equations. The investigation focuses on the potential of quantum entanglement to drastically reduce computational complexity and enhance the performance of quantum algorithms.

abstract: This paper introduces an Adaptive Self-Synchronous Quantum State Model, a novel approach to quantum computing that leverages quantum state self-adaptations to achieve stable and synchronized quantum states. Our model employs a dynamically adjusted evolution rate to ensure the quantum state remains in a stable state, offering a significant advancement over existing approaches. This research explores the design principles and implementation details of this model, providing a foundation for more robust and reliable quantum computations. We present a theoretical framework and initial implementation demonstrating the model's potential to mitigate decoherence issues inherent in current quantum systems.

title: Adaptive Kernel Learning via Variational Autoencoders
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to kernel learning, termed Adaptive Kernel Learning via Variational Autoencoders (AKLV). The core idea is to leverage the power of variational autoencoders (VAEs) to dynamically learn and adapt kernel function parameters. Traditional kernel methods often rely on manually designed or pre-defined kernels, which can be suboptimal for datasets with varying distributions. The AKLV framework addresses this limitation by allowing the kernel to evolve in response to the data itself. A VAE is trained to encode data into a latent space and subsequently decode it back, with the learned parameters of the kernel function directly influenced by the VAE's latent representation. This iterative process enables the kernel to adjust its shape and sensitivity, optimizing for the specific characteristics of the current data. The paper details the theoretical foundations, the proposed architecture, and outlines the key components of the AKLV system. The results demonstrate the potential of this adaptive approach to outperform static kernel designs in scenarios with non-stationary or complex data distributions.

title: Title: Automated Constraint-Based Quantum Algorithm Design
abstract: The design of quantum algorithms is a complex and time-consuming process, traditionally reliant on human expertise and intuition. This paper explores a novel system, the "Constraint-Driven Quantum Evolution" (CDQE) technique, designed to automate this design process, offering a significant leap forward in algorithm creation. We introduce a method that iteratively refines a quantum algorithm based on a predefined set of constraints, significantly reducing the need for manual iteration and enabling the discovery of novel and efficient quantum solutions. The CDQE leverages a dynamic constraint system, allowing the algorithm to adapt to evolving problem requirements. The core mechanism centers around a continuous refinement process driven by constraint satisfaction, offering a fundamentally different approach to quantum algorithm design. We present a preliminary implementation demonstrating the effectiveness of this system in generating candidate quantum circuits, highlighting its potential to revolutionize algorithm development.

title: Quantum Entanglement Information Search Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel information search algorithm leveraging quantum entanglement to enhance data discovery in large datasets. Traditional search methods often struggle with the complexity of identifying subtle correlations, limiting their effectiveness in scenarios with substantial data volumes. We propose a quantum-inspired approach that exploits the unique properties of quantum entanglement to establish a dynamic, probabilistic search framework. The core mechanism involves constructing a 'entanglement-aware' search space, enabling rapid pattern identification and improved matching efficiency. This algorithm is designed to outperform classical search techniques by focusing on higher-dimensional correlations and minimizing the computational cost associated with exhaustive search. The paper details the algorithm's design, analysis of its performance, and potential applications in data analysis and pattern recognition. The focus is on demonstrating the practical benefits of quantum entanglement in a search context, specifically addressing challenges related to scale and speed.

title: 基于图神经网络的动态算法优化
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic algorithm optimization framework leveraging Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) to dynamically adjust the structure of optimization algorithms. Traditional optimization methods often rely on manual design of the search space and constraints, limiting flexibility and potentially hindering the discovery of optimal solutions. GNNs offer a powerful mechanism for automatically learning optimal graph structures and weightings, enabling algorithms to adapt to varying environments and constraints. We propose a new approach that utilizes a GNN to represent the problem space as a graph, incorporating real-time feedback to refine the graph structure and optimize the algorithm's performance. The core mechanism focuses on dynamically adjusting the graph's connectivity and weights to effectively explore the solution space, leading to improved efficiency and robustness. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through a series of simulations and experiments, showcasing its ability to outperform traditional optimization techniques in a diverse range of problems.

title: Resilient Neural Networks via Distributed Laplacian Regularization
abstract: Deep neural networks have achieved remarkable success in various domains, but their vulnerability to adversarial attacks and data corruption remains a significant concern. This paper introduces a novel regularization technique, Distributed Laplacian Regularization (DLR), designed to enhance the robustness of deep neural networks. The core idea is to leverage the network's connectivity structure to enforce a robust and geometrically diverse weight distribution. DLR utilizes the distributed Laplacian operator, which captures the local connectivity patterns within the network, as a regularization term. This approach fundamentally differs from existing regularization methods, which often focus on individual weight updates or global loss minimization. Mathematical formulations are presented to detail the DLR term and its integration into the training process. The results demonstrate that DLR significantly improves the network's resilience to adversarial perturbations and noisy data, leading to improved accuracy and stability. The key contributions of this work are the introduction of the DLR regularization term and a theoretical understanding of how graph-theoretic properties can be used to enhance network robustness.

title: Self-Referential Formal Logic for AI Verification
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to AI verification using a self-referential formal logic system. The core idea is to create a logic with a dedicated "meta-inference" engine designed to continuously verify the logic's own axioms and inference rules. This creates a recursive verification loop, allowing for the detection and correction of inconsistencies within the logic itself. The system's robustness and trustworthiness are significantly enhanced through this self-assessment capability. The primary contribution lies in the development of a mechanism that facilitates continuous refinement of the logical framework, addressing potential vulnerabilities and improving overall reliability—a critical requirement for increasingly complex AI systems. This approach moves beyond traditional static verification methods, offering a dynamic and adaptive system for ensuring the soundness of AI reasoning. The system's architecture leverages a separation of concerns, with one engine dedicated to standard logical inference and another dedicated to the meta-inference process. This design promotes modularity and simplifies maintenance. This paper outlines the key components of the proposed system and discusses its potential implications for AI verification and trustworthiness.

title: Black-striped Squirrel Algorithm: A Novel Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of *Sitta neglecta*
abstract: This paper presents the Black-striped Squirrel Algorithm (BSA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of *Sitta neglecta*, a small squirrel species known for its unique and efficient foraging strategies. The BSA leverages the squirrel's ability to exploit and patch-follow, combined with a dynamic exploration-exploitation balance, to effectively search for optimal solutions in complex problem spaces. The algorithm incorporates key elements of the squirrel's behavior, including a modified roulette wheel selection mechanism, a patch-following strategy based on gradient information, and a dynamic adjustment of the exploration and exploitation parameters. Experimental results on a range of benchmark optimization problems demonstrate that the BSA exhibits competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as the Genetic Algorithm and the Particle Swarm Optimization. The algorithm's simplicity and adaptability make it a promising candidate for various optimization applications.

abstract: Quantum Entanglement Semantic Network (QESN) is a novel semantic network architecture leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement to enhance information transfer and knowledge reasoning. We present a comprehensive analysis of the network's operation, emphasizing the role of entanglement as a fundamental building block for improved cognitive processing. The research focuses on demonstrating the network's ability to achieve superior accuracy and speed in tasks requiring complex reasoning and pattern recognition, ultimately pushing the boundaries of semantic network capabilities.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Program Synthesis via Reinforcement Learning and Semantic Grammars
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to neuro-symbolic program synthesis that combines the strengths of reinforcement learning (RL) with formal semantic grammars. Traditional neuro-symbolic systems often struggle with the challenge of translating high-level, human-readable semantic specifications into executable code efficiently and reliably. Our methodology addresses this limitation by employing RL to train a system capable of generating code that adheres to a pre-defined, formal semantic grammar. This grammar serves as a constraint and guide, ensuring that the generated code is both syntactically correct and semantically aligned with the intended specification. The core of our system utilizes a reward function derived from the semantic grammar to guide the RL agent's learning process. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a theoretical framework, outlining the key components and potential benefits. The integration of a formally defined grammar provides a significantly more controlled and understandable code generation process compared to purely neural approaches, offering a pathway towards more robust and verifiable program synthesis. The key contribution lies in creating a dynamic synergy between the exploration capabilities of RL and the precision of semantic grammars.

title: ## Big-eared Flying Fox: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Big-eared Flying Fox" (BeFF), inspired by the foraging behavior of *Megabates tristis*, a large bat species known for its efficient and adaptable foraging strategies. The algorithm leverages the bat's echolocation and flight patterns to create a robust search process. BeFF utilizes a combination of a particle swarm optimization (PSO) core and a dynamically adjusted exploration-exploitation balance mimicking the bat's shift in search strategy based on food availability. Specifically, the algorithm employs a "pulse-echo" mechanism analogous to echolocation, where particles adjust their positions based on the perceived "echo" (fitness value) of neighboring particles. Furthermore, a novel "territory maintenance" mechanism is introduced, reflecting the bats' tendency to defend preferred foraging areas. The performance of BeFF is evaluated through a series of benchmark problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in achieving global optima and exhibiting superior convergence rates compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as PSO and Genetic Algorithm (GA). The algorithm's adaptability and efficiency make it a promising candidate for a wide range of optimization problems.

title: # Big Hairy Armadillo: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Armadillo Behavior
abstract: This paper introduces Big Hairy Armadillo (BHA), a novel metaheuristic algorithm designed to address complex optimization problems. The algorithm is inspired by the foraging behavior of the big hairy armadillo, specifically its unique method of digging for food. BHA incorporates elements of particle swarm optimization (PSO) and a simulated annealing (SA) approach, coupled with a novel adaptive inertia weight mechanism and a modified convergence criterion. The algorithm's core innovation lies in mimicking the armadillo's selective digging strategy, where it prioritizes areas with higher potential rewards based on a dynamic evaluation function. The performance of BHA is evaluated through a series of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and competitiveness compared to established metaheuristic algorithms. The results indicate that BHA exhibits robust performance across diverse problem landscapes, suggesting its potential for practical applications in various fields. Key performance metrics such as convergence rate, solution quality, and computational efficiency are analyzed, highlighting the algorithm's strengths and areas for potential future enhancement.

title: Adaptive Neuron Dynamic Topology Network
abstract: This paper proposes a novel neural network architecture, the Adaptive Neuron Dynamic Topology Network (ANDTN), designed to emulate the adaptive topology of biological neural networks. The core concept revolves around a "neuron topology energy" metric, used to quantify the effectiveness of connections. Neurons dynamically adjust their connections based on this energy gradient, resulting in a self-organizing, self-healing, and task-optimized network topology. Unlike traditional fixed-structure neural networks, ANDTN dynamically adapts its structure to improve performance. The network achieves this by continuously evaluating and modifying its connections, effectively creating an optimal network topology for the given task. This approach addresses the limitations of static neural network designs by incorporating the biological inspiration of adaptive neural circuitry. The presented model offers a potential pathway for developing more efficient and robust neural networks capable of handling complex and evolving tasks.

title: Graph Neural Networks with Memory Networks for Long-Term Dependencies
abstract: This paper addresses the limitations of standard Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) in capturing long-term dependencies within graph structures. Traditional GNNs often struggle to propagate information effectively across distant nodes, hindering their ability to learn complex patterns that evolve over time. We propose a novel architecture integrating GNNs with Memory Networks (MemNets) to overcome this challenge. This integration allows nodes to maintain and access a historical memory, facilitating the learning of long-range dependencies. Our approach leverages the message-passing mechanism of GNNs for node feature aggregation while utilizing MemNets' hierarchical memory structure to store and retrieve relevant information from the past. The resulting model demonstrates improved performance in tasks requiring the understanding of temporal relationships within graphs, such as predicting node states over time or modeling dynamic network behavior. We outline the core claim, the core mechanism, and highlight the novelty of our approach in effectively modeling long-term dependencies in dynamic graphs.

title: Dynamic Graph Embedding Learning via Evolutionary Algorithms
abstract: Graph embedding techniques have become increasingly important in various domains, including social network analysis, recommendation systems, and knowledge graph reasoning. However, most existing graph embedding methods are static, meaning they generate embeddings that remain fixed once trained, failing to adapt to changes in the underlying graph structure and node attributes over time. This paper proposes a novel dynamic graph embedding learning framework that leverages evolutionary algorithms to continuously refine graph embedding vectors. The framework incorporates both graph structural information and node attribute data as fitness components within the evolutionary process, enabling adaptive embedding generation. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through a theoretical analysis and a detailed description of the framework, outlining its key components and the evolutionary algorithm's role in optimizing the embeddings. title: Non-Structured Data Analysis Adaptive Clustering
abstract: This paper introduces a novel adaptive clustering algorithm designed to effectively identify hidden patterns within complex, non-structured data. Traditional clustering methods often struggle with data heterogeneity and require manual configuration of parameters, limiting their adaptability. Our proposed algorithm leverages the inherent properties of non-structured data – such as inherent correlations and dependencies – to automatically discover and refine cluster assignments, resulting in more accurate and insightful groupings. The core mechanism centers on a dynamic adjustment of cluster centroids and distance metrics based on the data's observed structure, enabling a more robust and flexible clustering process. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of experiments comparing it to established clustering techniques on diverse datasets. The results showcase the algorithm's superior performance in identifying complex patterns and generating higher-quality clusters compared to existing methods.

title: Australian Sealion: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Australian Sea Lions
abstract: This paper presents Australian Sealion (AS), a newly developed metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the behavioral patterns of Australian sea lions. AS combines elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO) to create a robust and efficient algorithm for solving complex optimization problems. The core mechanism of AS is based on the sea lion's hunting strategy – the 'coordinated search' – where individuals mimic the movement of the alpha sea lion, exploiting both local and global information. The algorithm incorporates a dynamic weight adjustment mechanism, mimicking the sea lions' ability to prioritize targets based on their perceived importance. Mathematical formulations describing the key components of AS, including the velocity update equation and the position update equation, are detailed. The performance of AS is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its competitive capability against established metaheuristic algorithms. The algorithm's adaptive nature and the incorporation of behavioral insights lead to improved convergence rates and solution quality. Keywords: Metaheuristic Algorithm, Particle Swarm Optimization, Grey Wolf Optimization, Australian Sea Lions, Hunting Strategy, Adaptive Weighting.

title: ## The Jumping Spider Inspired Adaptive Search Algorithm (JISA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Jumping Spider Inspired Adaptive Search Algorithm (JISA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the unique hunting strategies of jumping spiders. Jumping spiders are renowned for their precise movements, rapid adjustments, and ability to quickly adapt to changing environments. JISA leverages these characteristics through a dynamically adjusting exploration-exploitation balance, a multi-dimensional adaptive step size mechanism, and a novel 'stalking' strategy for candidate solution selection. The algorithm's core components, including the adaptive step size control, the stalking mechanism, and the probability-based selection, are designed to mimic the jumping spider's efficient and targeted search behavior. The algorithm's performance is evaluated theoretically, outlining its potential advantages and limitations.

title: Asian Straight-tusked Elephant-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed as the Asian Straight-tusked Elephant-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (ASE-MHA), motivated by the foraging behavior of Asian straight-tusked elephants (Elephas maximus maximus). These elephants exhibit remarkable strategies for locating scarce resources, particularly water, in challenging environments. The algorithm leverages key aspects of their behavior, including exploration, exploitation, and social learning, to effectively tackle complex optimization problems. The core of ASE-MHA utilizes a population-based search strategy, mimicking the elephants' movement patterns and resource selection. Specifically, the algorithm incorporates a novel 'Foraging Range' mechanism, inspired by the elephants' adaptive range selection based on resource availability, and a 'Social Learning' component that simulates the elephants' tendency to learn from each other's successful foraging locations. We demonstrate the algorithm's efficacy through theoretical analysis and simulations on a variety of benchmark optimization problems, including the Rosenbrock function, Rastrigin function, and the Sphere function. The results show that ASE-MHA consistently outperforms or achieves comparable performance to established metaheuristic algorithms like the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) in terms of convergence speed and solution quality. Future research will focus on adapting the algorithm for real-world applications and investigating its performance with diverse problem landscapes.

title: ## The Corvus Morphosis Algorithm: Inspired by the Flight Patterns of Raven Butterflies
abstract: This paper introduces the Corvus Morphosis Algorithm (CMA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior and flight patterns observed in Raven butterflies ( *Papilio corvus*). CMA leverages the butterfly's ability to dynamically adjust its flight path based on environmental factors, particularly food source availability and wind conditions, to navigate a complex search space. The algorithm incorporates three key components: a dynamic movement strategy mimicking the butterfly's 'morphosis' – continuous reshaping of its flight trajectory; a probabilistic wind influence model that simulates the impact of environmental variables on movement; and a food source density estimation method based on particle evaluation. CMA's core mechanism involves iteratively updating particle positions and velocities, guided by these simulated environmental cues. The aim is to establish a robust and adaptive optimization approach, suitable for a range of challenges where dynamic environmental considerations are paramount. This paper details the algorithm's theoretical framework, operational rules, and potential applications.

title: ## Red-crowned Crane Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (RCI-MOA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Red-crowned Crane Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (RCI-MOA), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior and navigation strategies of *Grus japonica* (Red-crowned Crane). The algorithm leverages the crane's ability to dynamically adjust its flight path based on environmental factors and social interactions, mimicking its efficient search process for food sources. RCI-MOA incorporates key mechanisms such as adaptive obstacle avoidance, flocking behavior, and a dynamic exploration-exploitation balance, all designed to enhance the algorithm's robustness and convergence speed. The core of the algorithm lies in a modified version of the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) framework, where each particle's movement is influenced by both its own best position and the collective knowledge of the flock, dynamically adjusting its velocity and acceleration based on perceived environmental challenges. This paper outlines the algorithm's design, mathematical formulation, and potential applications, highlighting its unique approach to metaheuristic optimization.

title: Quantum Entanglement Modeling of Non-Linear Geometry
abstract: This paper explores the application of quantum entanglement to the modeling of non-linear geometry. We propose a novel framework centered around a quantum entanglement-based geometric model, capable of dynamically adapting geometric shapes through self-induced transformations, leveraging the inherent non-linearity of quantum states. The core mechanism involves constructing a quantum entangled state representation of the geometric form, utilizing the non-linear properties of entanglement to enable self-consistent geometric evolution. This approach aims to deliver high-precision geometric modeling and deformation, offering a fundamentally new perspective on geometric computation. The investigation will detail the mathematical formulation of the model, the implementation of the entanglement-based transformation process, and the resulting geometric transformations, emphasizing the potential for high accuracy and dynamic shaping.

title: Antarctic Fur Seal Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the Antarctic Fur Seal Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (AFIMA), designed to tackle complex optimization problems. The algorithm's design is fundamentally inspired by the foraging behavior of Antarctic fur seals, specifically their innovative strategies for locating food sources in challenging, unpredictable environments. AFIMA utilizes a multi-layered exploration and exploitation process mimicking the seal's movement patterns, incorporating elements of both local search and global search. The core components of the algorithm include a position representation based on a ring structure, a movement mechanism modeled after seal's navigational strategies, and an adaptive inertia weight scheme reflecting the seals' responsiveness to environmental changes. Performance evaluations are conducted on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating AFIMA's competitive capabilities against established metaheuristic algorithms such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The algorithm's ability to adapt and adjust its search strategy based on the problem landscape is a key factor in its effectiveness. This research contributes a new approach to metaheuristic optimization, offering a potentially valuable tool for solving intricate optimization challenges across various domains.

abstract: This paper introduces the Polar Shrimp Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (PSIMA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of polar shrimp. Polar shrimp exhibit remarkable adaptive strategies for resource acquisition in challenging Arctic environments. PSIMA leverages these strategies – including directional movement, localized exploration, and dynamic adjustment of search parameters – to effectively explore complex search spaces. The algorithm employs a population-based approach, where each individual represents a potential solution. Movement is governed by a polar coordinate system, utilizing both radial and angular components to guide the search. The algorithm dynamically adjusts its parameters, mimicking the shrimp's responsiveness to environmental changes. This paper details the algorithm's theoretical framework, design principles, and potential applications. The aim is to provide a robust and adaptable optimization method suitable for a wide range of problems.

title: Bio-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems: The Frog Leap Algorithm (FLA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Frog Leap Algorithm (FLA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of American bullfrogs. The algorithm leverages the frog's ability to leap, adjust its leap direction, and navigate complex environments to effectively explore and converge towards optimal solutions in complex optimization problems. FLA utilizes a population of frogs, each represented by position (s_i) and velocity (v_i), where 'i' denotes the individual frog. The algorithm employs a leap-based movement strategy, incorporating adaptive leap direction determination and a 'leap adjustment' mechanism based on the gradient of the objective function. Furthermore, FLA incorporates a 'leap frequency' parameter to control exploration versus exploitation, and a 'leap radius' to limit the search space. This paper details the algorithm's formulation, key parameters, and its potential application across various optimization challenges. The core innovation lies in the dynamic adjustment of leap parameters, mimicking the frog's intelligent decision-making process. The algorithm aims to provide a robust and efficient alternative to existing metaheuristic methods.

title: Dynamic Particle Quantum Computing: A Novel Approach to Quantum Algorithm Optimization and Expansion
abstract: Quantum computing holds immense promise for revolutionizing various fields, from drug discovery to materials science. However, the development of practical quantum algorithms is hindered by the need for sophisticated optimization and expansion techniques. This paper introduces a novel quantum computing framework, Dynamic Particle Quantum Computing (DPQC), leveraging dynamic particle models to dynamically adjust quantum algorithms, thereby optimizing their performance and expanding their applicability. We detail the framework's design, key mechanisms, and potential benefits. Our analysis demonstrates the significant advantages of DPQC over traditional approaches in optimizing and extending quantum algorithms.

title: ## The Purple-Chested Thrush Metaheuristic: A Novel Optimization Algorithm Inspired by Avian Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper introduces the Purple-Chested Thrush Metaheuristic (PCTM), a novel optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging strategies of *Catharus corinthians*, a bird known for its efficient and adaptable search behavior. PCTM leverages the observed characteristics of thrush foraging – including zone-based searching, adaptive step sizes, and a dynamic exploration-exploitation balance – to create a robust metaheuristic approach. The algorithm employs a 'zone' concept to represent the search space, dynamically adjusts step sizes based on the perceived density of potential solutions, and incorporates a 'foraging pressure' parameter to control the balance between exploration and exploitation. The core of PCTM lies in its 'resonance' mechanism, which mimics the thrush's ability to identify and converge upon promising regions within the search space. This paper details the algorithm's theoretical foundation, its key components, and proposes a conceptual framework for its application to various optimization problems. The aim is to present a computationally efficient and adaptable metaheuristic algorithm with potential for improvement in complex optimization tasks.

title: Core Claim: Design a self-adaptive topological quantum computing framework for predicting quantum system evolution, and provide more effective quantum algorithm design.
abstract: Quantum computing offers the potential for exponentially faster computations compared to classical computers, but the design and optimization of quantum algorithms remain a significant challenge. This research explores a novel approach to quantum system evolution prediction using a self-adaptive topological framework. We propose a dynamic modeling strategy that leverages topology to represent the evolution of quantum states, allowing for the prediction of complex quantum behavior. The framework incorporates a continuous, self-consistent evolution process, enabling the identification of key transition points and the generation of more effective quantum algorithms. This work represents a significant advancement in quantum system dynamics prediction, offering a robust and adaptable methodology for exploring and designing new quantum algorithms. The core of our approach lies in the creation of a self-adaptive topology that evolves alongside the quantum system, providing a dynamic and predictive tool. This dynamic evolution, coupled with our modeling approach, promises to significantly enhance the efficiency and versatility of quantum computation. Specifically, we demonstrate the framework's ability to accurately predict the behavior of various quantum systems, including those exhibiting complex entanglement dynamics, opening doors to the development of novel quantum algorithms.

title: Alpine Marmot Optimization Algorithm (AMOA)
abstract: This paper presents the Alpine Marmot Optimization Algorithm (AMOA), a novel metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of Alpine Marmots. AMOA utilizes a combination of exploration and exploitation strategies mimicking the marmot's characteristic movement patterns – searching for food in a territory, marking favored locations, and strategically relocating based on food availability and perceived risk. The algorithm incorporates three key components: a territory division mechanism, a marking strategy based on fitness values, and a relocation mechanism influenced by both food density and distance to previously marked locations. Mathematical formulations are provided to describe each component, including the territory division probability, the marking intensity, and the relocation probability. The performance of AMOA is evaluated through numerical experiments on benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time. The algorithm's adaptability and potential for application in various complex optimization scenarios are discussed. title: Non-Linear Differential Equation Optimization Algorithm
abstract: This paper presents a novel algorithm for non-linear differential equation optimization, designed to adaptively adjust optimization targets based on dynamic input data. Traditional optimization methods often rely on static parameter adjustments, limiting their applicability to static systems. Our proposed algorithm leverages a "non-linear constraint optimization" mechanism to dynamically modify optimization objectives in response to real-time data changes, effectively avoiding local optima and enabling more intelligent optimization. This approach offers a significant improvement in performance compared to existing methods, particularly in scenarios with evolving input dynamics. The core mechanism focuses on creating a feedback loop that continuously monitors input data and adjusts the constraints to steer the optimization process toward global optima. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this algorithm through a series of simulations and experimental results, showcasing its ability to handle complex, dynamic parameter spaces.

title: A Natural Language Processing Approach to Document-based Question Answering
abstract: DocuMind is a document-based question answering system built entirely on classical NLP techniques, without relying on deep learning.It combines TF-IDF vectorization with cosine similarity to locate relevant passages within uploaded documents (PDF, TXT, DOCX), then applies rule-based logic to extract precise answers based on question type-WHO, WHEN, WHERE, WHY, HOW MANY, WHAT, and YES/NO.Deployed as a Flask web application, the system delivers real-time answers with confidence scores and links back to source context for verification.Evaluation across diverse documents shows that DocuMind achieves solid retrieval precision and fast memory performance, demonstrating that lightweight, feature-engineered NLP approaches remain a practical and efficient alternative to deep learning for document-based question answering.
