title: BALANCED DETECTION OF ANOMALOUS TRANSACTIONS USING HYBRID AWRED ON REAL DATA UNDER STRONG CLASS IMBALANCE
abstract: The article considered the problem of detecting anomalous transactions in strongly imbalanced financial data. These data included a very small amount of the rare class compared with the number of normal operations. Such formulation was difficult not only because of the small number of anomalous examples. It was also caused by the fact that part of suspicious transactions did not form a clearly separated group in the feature space, therefore the usual reconstruction error of the autoencoder did not always provide sufficient ranking quality and reliable threshold selection. To solve this problem, the seventh version of the HYBRID AWRED method was used. It applies a hybrid approach in which the autoencoder reconstruction basis is combined with a stable profile of calibrated residuals.All experiments were carried out on the Credit Card Fraud Detection dataset, which included 284807 transactions, 30 features and 492 anomalous records. The share of the anomalous class was only 0.1727%. The training sample was formed only from normal transactions. The validation sample was used for threshold selection and parameter tuning of HYBRID AWRED v7, and the test sample was used only for the final quality evaluation. This approach reduced the risk of information leakage from the test data into the threshold tuning procedure.In the HYBRID AWRED v7 method, fixed calibration of reconstruction residuals was used after the initial training of the autoencoder. For each feature, a calibrated residual was calculated, after which its positive part was taken and then soft logarithmic compression ln (1 + rj +) was applied. This reduced the influence of too large values in the right tail of the anomaly score. The final score was formed as a normalized linear combination of the calibrated residual profile with non-negative weights. The AWRED component was trained using pseudo-anomalies and a ranking loss function. Such approach made it possible not only to reduce reconstruction errors, but also to improve the ordering of normal and anomalous transactions by risk level.According to the results of five independent runs, HYBRID AWRED v7 achieved AUC-ROC 0.9432+/-0.0117, AUC-PR 0.6639+/-0.0634, F1 0.7153+/-0.0402, MCC 0.7180+/-0.0399, Precision 0.6608+/-0.0565 and Recall 0.7831+/-0.0501. Compared with such competitors as AE, AE-finetuned, DAE, SVDD and DAGMM, the proposed approach showed the best quality by AUC-PR, F1, MCC and Recall. But it should be taken into account that this result should not be interpreted as a complete separation of anomalous transactions from normal ones. Part of weak suspicious transactions remains close to the normal profile. However, HYBRID AWRED v7 noticeably improved the practically important threshold quality in the task with extreme class imbalance. Keywords: anomalous transactions, anomaly detection, autoencoder, HYBRID AWRED v7, AUC-PR, class imbalance, calibrated residuals, threshold decision.

title: The Impact of Signal Deletion in Text Preprocessing on Timestamp Comment Detection under Severe Class Imbalance
abstract: Timestamping in YouTube comment sections is a distinctive form of participatory content curation. This study examines why four text classification algorithms, namely Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machine, Random Forest, and XGBoost, fail completely at detecting timestamp-bearing comments in an informal Indonesian-language corpus. Across 14,149 comments from Ruangguru Clash of Champions videos, the imbalance ratio reaches 73.86:1. Every model returns an accuracy near 98.7% with a minority-class recall of zero, a Balanced Accuracy of 0.50, and Cohen’s Kappa at or below zero, the textbook signature of the Accuracy Paradox. The contribution is diagnostic: class imbalance is not the sole cause. A token-level trace shows that punctuation removal followed by standalone-numeral removal deterministically destroys the pattern defining the positive label, while sparse-term pruning at a 0.99 threshold discards vocabulary occurring in fewer than 1% of documents, above the minority prevalence of 1.34%. Recovering the confusion matrices permits a complete imbalance-robust metric set to be computed, confirming that all four models are indistinguishable from a constant classifier that ignores its input. The study specifies the ablation required to separate these causes, and establishes that before minority-class failure is attributed to imbalance, researchers must verify that preprocessing has not deleted the signal being learned.

title: A medical image classification algorithm based on a hierarchical and complementary attention-enhanced Swin Transformer model
abstract: Abstract With the rapid development of precision medicine and intelligent diagnostic technologies, automatic medical image classification has become an important tool for assisting clinical decision-making. However, substantial variations in lesion scale, complex long-range dependencies of tissue structures, and the need to capture subtle anatomical features present significant challenges to existing deep learning models. To address the limitations of the Swin Transformer in modeling multi-scale lesions and multi-level feature interactions, this study proposes a hierarchical complementary feature enhancement framework based on the Swin Transformer for medical image classification. The proposed architecture performs collaborative feature learning at three representation levels, including macro-scale lesion perception, global contextual interaction, and local detail refinement. Specifically, a Multi-scale Depthwise SE Block (MSD-SE Block) is introduced at the input of each stage of the Swin Transformer to enhance the model’s multi-scale feature representation capability. Subsequently, a Residual Convolutional Attention (RCA) module is integrated following the self-attention mechanism and the Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) to strengthen global contextual modeling, while a Local Detail Enhanced Residual Channel-Spatial Attention (LDERCSA) module is employed to refine subtle anatomical structures and discriminative local features. Through the coordinated interaction of these components, the proposed framework establishes a hierarchical feature enhancement mechanism that effectively improves medical image representation across multiple scales and feature levels. Comprehensive experiments were conducted on eight core subsets of MedMNIST v2, including BloodMNIST, BreastMNIST, DermaMNIST, OCTMNIST, OrganSMNIST, PathMNIST, PneumoniaMNIST, and RetinaMNIST, using an input resolution of 224 $$\times$$ 224. Single-module comparison and ablation studies demonstrate that each proposed component contributes positively to the overall performance. Experimental results show that the proposed model achieves significant performance improvements on BreastMNIST, OCTMNIST, OrganSMNIST, and PneumoniaMNIST. Furthermore, comparative evaluations across all datasets confirm that the proposed framework exhibits strong robustness and generalization capability when processing multiple medical imaging modalities, including ultrasound, CT, X-ray, endoscopic, and microscopic images, thereby providing reliable technical support for computer-aided medical diagnosis systems.

title: MELON: A Large-Scale Dataset for Multi-Event Text-to-Long-Video Retrieval
abstract: Existing text-video retrieval datasets primarily consist of short-form clips containing a single dominant event. While suitable for measuring basic vision-language alignment, they are limited in capturing real-world retrieval scenarios, where long-form videos naturally contain multiple semantically distinct events and a single text query may correspond to several non-contiguous temporal segments. To bridge this gap, we introduce MELON, the first large-scale dataset designed to extend text-video retrieval to long-form videos featuring complex, multi-event structures. MELON explicitly annotates multiple event intervals per video along with their corresponding textual descriptions, enabling both training and evaluation of multi-event understanding in long, untrimmed videos. In addition, we propose a multi-event aware loss that encourages models to differentiate between full-event and partial-event matches, yielding substantial improvements in retrieval accuracy. Together, the MELON dataset and our proposed loss establish a robust foundation for expanding text-to-video retrieval to complex long-form scenarios and provide a more realistic evaluation setting for future research in the field.

title: Faster Than Flash: Exploiting Attention Sparsity for Efficient Long-Context Decoding
abstract: The development of long-context Large Language Models (LLMs) is constrained by the memory bandwidth bottleneck and quadratic complexity of the attention mechanism during decoding. To overcome the inherent trade-offs between the memory overhead of metadata-based metrics and the computational inefficiency of adaptive selection strategies, we present Faster Flash Decoding (FFD), a novel hardware-algorithm co-design framework designed to break the memory wall in long-context decoding. FFD integrates the selector and computer into a fully fused kernel, replacing external metadata indices with content-aware scanning via low-bit quantization. Furthermore, we introduce the top-delta strategy, which dynamically filters blocks to achieve distribution-adaptive sparsity without global synchronization. Offering a training-free and plug-and-play solution, FFD also enables the reuse of scanning results for computation, achieving up to 11.6x kernel-level speedup and scaling to 256K context length, with 2.37x end-to-end throughput improvement. Empirical validation on RULER and LongBench confirms that FFD maintains model accuracy while delivering high-ratio sparsity, with code available at https://github.com/qluoluo/faster-flash-decoding

title: PRIME: Mitigating Subgroup Optimization Competition in Shared CTR Top Networks with Plug-in Residual Input-Conditioned Mixture of Expert
abstract: Click-through rate (CTR) models vary in feature-interaction design, yet their top networks usually remain a single multilayer perceptron shared by all examples. Heterogeneous user, item, and context subgroups therefore update the same parameters; weakly aligned learning signals make the aggregate gradient a compromise among competing directions. We study the competition on Avazu with 4 models and 4 semantic fields. Across all architectures, semantic subgroups show lower Top-NN gradient cosine similarity than random groups matched by sample size and label ratio, with reductions of 0.23-0.37. This competition motivates input-conditioned experts, but directly replacing an established Dense mapping changes its initial function, sharing pattern, and capacity, obscuring the source of gains. We introduce PRIME (Plug-in Residual Input-conditioned Mixture of Experts), a Dense-anchored mixture of low-rank residual experts. PRIME anchors the original prediction and uses zero-residual initialization to match the Dense baseline exactly at training onset. Input-dependent routing weights low-rank experts for example-specific logit corrections; multi-bag aggregation and EMA load biases stabilize conditional estimation. We evaluate PRIME on held-out Avazu and Criteo test sets across 13 CTR architectures and five paired seeds. Median paired AUC gains are +0.0022 and +0.0066, with LogLoss reductions of 0.0011 and 0.0081, respectively. On FiBiNET and DCNv2, PRIME outperforms APG in all ten seed-level AUC comparisons while using fewer parameters and lower inference latency on both backbones. These results show that function-preserving conditional residuals add input-dependent capacity while preserving the Dense path and its optimization stability. Code is available at https://github.com/YH-learning/PRIME.

title: Penggunaan Logika Fuzzy Metode Mamdani untuk Mengetahui Tingkat Kepuasan Mahasiswa Terhadap Pelayanan Tenaga Kependidikan di Universitas Balikpapan
abstract: The quality of service provided by educational support staff is a crucial aspect of the student academic experience. At Balikpapan University, these services are delivered by administrative staff in faculties, laboratories, and the library. While measuring satisfaction using a Likert scale offers an overview of student ratings, its categorical nature can limit the representation of satisfaction levels, which are inherently gradual. This study aims to analyze student satisfaction levels regarding educational support staff services using the Mamdani fuzzy inference method. Data were collected from 53 active students via a 15-item questionnaire and grouped into three input variables: services provided by faculty, laboratory, and library staff. Each variable was represented by four linguistic sets—dissatisfied, less satisfied, satisfied, and very satisfied—with membership boundaries calibrated based on empirical minimum and maximum scores. The inference process employed max-min composition and the centroid defuzzification method. The analysis revealed high satisfaction levels across all three service aspects, and the overall defuzzification results classified respondents into categories ranging from "Satisfied" to "Very Satisfied." These findings demonstrate that the Mamdani fuzzy approach can effectively represent gradual levels of student satisfaction and yield a more structured classification of questionnaire data.

title: TITLE: A Multi-Scale Novel Neural Networks Learning Algorithms Optimization Framework
abstract: ABSTRACTThis research operates on a singular, elegant identity axiom: a localized environment is fundamentally identical to its absolute matrix of latent information potential ((Equ,1)): (E ≡ I_Abs). By treating energy gradients and informational structures as the exact same physical property, we establish a universal framework for predicting structural failure modes before they occur. To execute this theory, we introduce the Neural Networks Learning Algorithms optimization framework, a continuous-time physics-informed mapping pipeline. Rather than treating raw streaming data as flat, isolated sequences, this architecture bridges the gap between machine learning and physical laws by binding a 50,433-parameter Neural Network directly to a 16-equation governing system matrix. Crucially, the 16 equations and the 50,433 parameters are parts of the exact same computational body. The physics equations do not run side-by-side with the network; they are baked directly into the hidden layers, forward-propagation equations, and output branches of the Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) engine. An Informational Topology Collapse is formally defined as a non-linear phase transition under acute phase-space volume constriction ((Equ,2)): (V_eff → 0). The failure occurs when local processing nodes completely uncouple from global tracking coordinates. Topologically, this mimics an elementary simplicial collapse where multi-scale structural loops—measured mathematically by independent network Betti numbers (beta_k(t))—instantly dissolve to zero ((Equ,3)): (beta_k(t) → 0), eliminating higher-dimensional systemic connectivity.

title: K-Score: A Time-Aware, Exam-Weighted Readiness Model and Scheduling Framework for Adaptive KEAM Preparation
abstract: Preparation for multiple-choice entrance examinations requires more than measuring aggregate accuracy. A useful student model must distinguish broad from narrow practice, recent knowledge from stale knowledge, easy-item success from difficult-item success, and conceptual weakness from time-pressure or careless errors. It must also convert diagnosis into an actionable study schedule while resisting score inflation from low-stakes practice or low-integrity testing. This paper proposes K-Score, an interpretable, time-aware and exam-weighted readiness framework for the Kerala Engineering Architecture Medical (KEAM) engineering entrance examination. The framework represents each chapter through three complementary components: coverage of its knowledge components, difficulty-adjusted performance including response-time evidence, and predicted retention based on a personalized half-life. These components are combined into chapter mastery, aggregated using empirically smoothed chapter importance and the examination’s Mathematics–Physics–Chemistry blueprint, and mapped to a 0–1000 K-Score. Four interaction modes—practice, revision, chapter or subject testing, and full simulated examination—contribute evidence with different reliability. The framework separates active readiness, which can decay during inactivity, from verified readiness, which is refreshed by controlled assessments. A scheduling policy selects the next action using mastery gaps, retention risk, uncertainty, recurring error patterns, chapter importance, time to examination and available study time. evidence.title: K-Score: A Time-Aware, Exam-Weighted Readiness Model and Scheduling Framework for Adaptive KEAM Preparation
evidence.abstract: Preparation for multiple-choice entrance examinations requires more than measuring aggregate accuracy. A useful student model must distinguish broad from narrow practice, recent knowledge from stale knowledge, easy-item success from difficult-item success, and conceptual weakness from time-pressure or careless errors. It must also convert diagnosis into an actionable study schedule while resisting score inflation from low-stakes practice or low-integrity testing. This paper proposes K-Score, an interpretable, time-aware and exam-weighted readiness framework for the Kerala Engineering Architecture Medical (KEAM) engineering entrance examination. The framework represents each chapter through three complementary components: coverage of its knowledge components, difficulty-adjusted performance including response-time evidence, and predicted retention based on a personalized half-life. These components are combined into chapter mastery, aggregated using empirically smoothed chapter importance and the examination’s Mathematics–Physics–Chemistry blueprint, and mapped to a 0–1000 K-Score. Four interaction modes—practice, revision, chapter or subject testing, and full simulated examination—contribute evidence with different reliability. The framework separates active readiness, which can decay during inactivity, from verified readiness, which is refreshed by controlled assessments. A scheduling policy selects the next action using mastery gaps, retention risk, uncertainty, recurring error patterns, chapter importance, time to examination and available study time. We also specify cold-start handling, test-form equating, confidence reporting, integrity-aware leaderboards and a validation protocol. The contribution is a methodological and system-design proposal; empirical effectiveness on student outcomes remains to be established through offline calibration and prospective controlled studies.

abstract: Quantum state transfer is a fundamental challenge in quantum computing, demanding efficient and robust methods for navigating complex quantum states. We introduce a new approach that dynamically manipulates quantum states using geometric transformations, aiming to significantly reduce the computational cost associated with state transfer. The core mechanism involves strategically applying geometric transformations that guide the state transfer, optimizing the transition process and ultimately enhancing the overall performance of quantum computation. This research explores the potential of geometric structuring as a tool for simplifying and accelerating state transfer, offering a promising pathway towards more efficient quantum algorithms. The investigation focuses on demonstrating the effectiveness of this algorithm through mathematical analysis and simulation, highlighting its advantages in terms of computational complexity and state fidelity. The results demonstrate a substantial improvement in transfer efficiency compared to existing state transfer methods, showcasing the potential of this geometric approach to revolutionize quantum state manipulation.

title: 基于自适应的量子信息加密算法
abstract: This paper presents a novel quantum information encryption algorithm based on adaptive quantum states. Traditional cryptographic systems rely on static key generation, making them vulnerable to attacks exploiting subtle variations in the key. This research introduces a new algorithm that dynamically adjusts the encryption key based on the quantum state, significantly enhancing security through continuous state analysis and adaptation. We detail the core mechanism, the algorithm's architecture, and the resulting security implications. The algorithm leverages quantum state dynamics to create a continuously evolving key, rendering traditional cryptanalysis significantly more challenging. This offers a promising pathway towards robust and adaptable cryptographic solutions.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel probabilistic model, termed "隐变量自适应的概率模型", designed to enhance model generalization through dynamic adjustment of its parameters based on the evolving states of hidden variables. title: Self-Referential Neural Networks for Intrinsic Representation Learning
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to intrinsic representation learning using self-referential neural networks. The core idea is to design a neural network architecture where the output of one or more layers is fed back as input to the same layer, creating a recursive loop. This self-referential mechanism allows the network to optimize its internal representations based on the information it's processing, effectively learning a representation that is inherently useful for the task. We posit that this approach differs significantly from traditional representation learning methods, which often rely on external signals or ground truth labels. The presented framework offers a potential pathway to more robust and adaptable representations by allowing the network to directly assess and refine its own internal state. The primary focus is on the theoretical foundations and architectural considerations of such networks, without experimental validation. We explore the mathematical formalization of this concept, outlining key equations and the iterative process involved. The aim is to provide a clear and concise description of a potentially transformative technique in the field of deep learning.

title: Quantum Entanglement for Non-Locality Information Encoding and Decoding
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, exhibits correlations that cannot be explained by local realism. This paper explores the potential of utilizing entangled states for information encoding and decoding, aiming to overcome the limitations imposed by the non-locality inherent in entanglement. We propose a novel approach that leverages entangled states to establish secure communication and data processing, incorporating a quantum decoding mechanism to mitigate potential vulnerabilities arising from entanglement's inherent properties. The core mechanism centers around encoding information via entangled states, followed by a carefully designed decoding process. We analyze the strengths and weaknesses of this method, highlighting its potential for secure information transfer and data manipulation. The paper concludes with a discussion of the challenges and future directions of this research.

title: Quantum Clocks Based on Entanglement
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum entanglement for constructing ultra-precise timekeeping devices, surpassing the limitations of classical clocks. The core concept involves leveraging the inherent correlations within entangled quantum states to achieve unprecedented temporal resolution. We detail a proposed architecture for a quantum entanglement clock, focusing on utilizing the phase-sensitive nature of entangled particles to perform time measurements. The theoretical framework demonstrates how entanglement can fundamentally alter time measurement, offering a pathway towards dramatically improved accuracy. This work highlights the significance of quantum mechanics in redefining the boundaries of precision measurement and opens new avenues for technological advancements in areas such as fundamental physics research, metrology, and navigation systems. This research presents a novel approach to timekeeping, moving beyond the constraints of classical mechanics and into the realm of quantum phenomena.

title: ## Black Wallaby: A Novel Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by Black Wallabies
abstract: This paper presents Black Wallaby, a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the unique foraging strategies of Black Wallabies. These marsupials exhibit remarkable adaptability and efficiency in navigating complex, multi-dimensional landscapes to locate food sources. Black Wallaby leverages these observed behaviors – particularly their ability to dynamically adjust step sizes, explore diverse regions, and consolidate promising areas – to create a robust optimization algorithm. The algorithm employs a novel population representation, a dynamic step size control mechanism, and a sophisticated convergence criterion based on both population diversity and individual fitness. We demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness across a range of benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its potential to outperform existing metaheuristic methods in terms of solution quality and convergence speed. The core of the algorithm revolves around the concept of "Wallaby Trails," representing promising search regions, and the "Wallaby Leap," a dynamic adjustment of the step size based on the trail's fitness and overall population distribution. The algorithm's performance is evaluated against established metaheuristic techniques like Genetic Algorithm and Particle Swarm Optimization, highlighting its advantages in challenging scenarios.

title: Title: Non-Standard Laplacian for Quantum Error Correction
abstract: Quantum error correction is a critical component of quantum information processing, enabling the reliable transmission and manipulation of quantum states. Current error correction codes face significant challenges due to the inherent noise present in quantum systems. This paper investigates a novel Laplacian operator designed to enhance the robustness of quantum error correction by leveraging geometric properties. We introduce a new Laplacian operator, characterized by specific geometric constraints, which exhibits improved resilience to noise compared to conventional Laplacian methods. The core mechanism focuses on mitigating the impact of quantum fluctuations by introducing a carefully crafted geometric structure within the operator. This leads to a potential advancement in quantum error correction strategies and improved fidelity of quantum computations. The implications of this work extend to the design of more reliable and efficient quantum systems.

title: Self-Supervised Learning for Graph Representation Learning with Contrastive Predictive Coding
abstract: This paper introduces a novel self-supervised learning framework for graph representation learning based on contrastive predictive coding (CPC). Traditional methods largely depend on contrastive learning, which often struggles to effectively model the intricate and dynamic relationships within graphs. Our approach leverages the principle of predictive coding, where nodes learn to anticipate future graph states. This allows for the creation of richer and more expressive latent representations. We formulate the learning process as a prediction task, where each node attempts to reconstruct its future neighbors within the graph. The core idea is to minimize the discrepancy between the predicted future states and the actual future states, thereby capturing the graph's underlying dynamics. We present a mathematical formulation outlining the key components of the framework, including the prediction loss and the latent representation learning objective. The proposed method demonstrates the potential to generate more informative graph embeddings compared to existing contrastive learning approaches, particularly in scenarios involving complex graph structures and evolving relationships.

abstract: This paper introduces a novel probabilistic regularization method designed to enhance the generalization and stability of deep learning models. Traditional regularization techniques often rely on fixed parameters, which struggle to effectively address complex data and model characteristics. title: Dynamic Context-Dependent Graph Learning (DCDGL)
abstract: This paper introduces Dynamic Context-Dependent Graph Learning (DCDGL), a novel framework for intelligent reasoning and decision-making in complex environments. DCDGL leverages a dynamic graph structure learned through adaptive graph modeling, enabling it to capture and utilize multi-dimensional contextual information in real-time. The system employs a probabilistic graph model with a dynamic graph construction and update mechanism, utilizing reinforcement learning to optimize the graph's topology and node attributes based on observed data and a defined objective. Unlike traditional rule-based or knowledge graph approaches, DCDGL dynamically adapts to changing contexts, offering superior performance in tasks requiring nuanced understanding and adaptability. The core claim is that through self-adaptive graph structure learning, the system can effectively capture and utilize multi-dimensional contextual information, significantly enhancing complex task reasoning and decision-making capabilities, surpassing traditional methods. The system's architecture incorporates a "context-aware" graph algorithm that actively adjusts graph topology and node associations based on dynamic environmental changes, mirroring human cognitive processes. This approach represents a fundamental shift in intelligent systems, moving beyond static representations to embrace dynamic, context-sensitive knowledge structures. ---

title: 基于量子自适应的图神经网络
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to graph neural networks (GNNs) – the 'Quantum Adaptive Graph Neural Network' – leveraging quantum self-adaptation to enhance both expressiveness and computational efficiency. Traditional GNNs often struggle with the inherent complexities of graph data and require substantial computational resources. We propose a new architecture that employs quantum mechanics to simulate graph structures, allowing the network to learn more robust representations. This approach, dubbed Quantum Adaptive Graph Neural Network (QAGNN), utilizes quantum machine learning algorithms to improve the network's ability to capture intricate relationships within the graph. The paper details the core mechanism, its mathematical foundations, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating significant improvements in various graph classification tasks compared to traditional GNNs. We present a comprehensive analysis of the QAGNN's performance and discuss potential future research directions.

title: Quantum-Inspired Entanglement-Based Data Compression
abstract: This paper investigates a novel approach to data compression inspired by the principles of quantum entanglement. Traditional data compression techniques often struggle to efficiently represent complex data patterns, particularly in scenarios with high redundancy. We propose an algorithm that utilizes the concept of entangled qubits to represent data, exploiting the strong correlations between these qubits to achieve potentially higher compression ratios. The core idea involves encoding data into a set of entangled qubits, where the state of one qubit directly influences the state of the others. This inherently creates a compact representation, reducing the overall data size. The algorithm is designed to be computationally efficient, aiming to mimic the core advantages of quantum mechanics without requiring full quantum computing resources. We explore the theoretical foundations of this approach, detailing the mathematical framework for qubit representation and the encoding/decoding processes. The paper highlights the potential advantages and challenges associated with this quantum-inspired method, suggesting future research directions and refinements.

title: ## Atlantic Forest Fringe-lipped Bat-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Fringe-lipped Bat" (FLB) algorithm, inspired by the foraging behavior of the Atlantic Forest fringe-lipped bat (Rhinolophus ligaei). These bats exhibit a unique hunting strategy characterized by intermittent flights, searching patterns, and adaptive adjustments based on environmental factors. The algorithm leverages these key characteristics to efficiently navigate complex optimization landscapes. The FLB algorithm incorporates three core components: a 'searching' phase mimicking the bat's exploration, a 'sensing' phase reflecting the bat's ability to detect food sources, and a 'decision' phase based on the bat's response to environmental cues. Mathematical formulations detailing these phases are presented, including the probability of searching (P_s), the sensing range (R), and the decision making function (D). The algorithm's performance is evaluated through simulations applied to several benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and adaptability. The key contributions of this work lie in the novel application of bat foraging behavior to metaheuristic design and the development of a computationally efficient algorithm capable of addressing a wide range of optimization challenges.

title: DIGITAL PATHOLOGY FOR CANCER DIAGNOSIS: DIAGNOSTIC CONCORDANCE WITH CONVENTIONAL MICROSCOPY: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW AND METAANALYSIS
abstract: Background: Whole-slide imaging (WSI) has transformed digital pathology from a consultation and archival tool into apotential platform for primary cancer diagnosis. Because oncologic histopathology directly determines tumor classification,grading, staging, margin status, and treatment, digital interpretation must demonstrate clinically acceptable concordance withconventional light microscopy (CLM). title: Automated Hardware Circuit Design Based on Genetic Algorithms
abstract: This paper investigates the application of genetic algorithms (GAs) for automating the design of complex hardware circuits. The core claim is that a GA can effectively optimize circuit performance and power consumption through an iterative, evolutionary process. The mechanism involves treating a hardware circuit as a biological entity with a defined "genome" represented by its structure and parameters. The GA then utilizes selection, crossover, and mutation operators to evolve this genome, progressively refining the circuit design. This approach differs from traditional hardware design methodologies, which primarily rely on human expertise and simulation-based optimization. By leveraging the global search capabilities of GAs, this research aims to provide a novel and automated pathway toward efficient and optimized hardware circuit design. This paper details the formulation of the design problem as a GA problem, explores key GA parameters, and presents a preliminary framework for its implementation. The focus is on demonstrating the potential of the method rather than a fully realized design automation system.

title: Annam Red-cheeked Squirrel: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Squirrel Behavior
abstract: This paper presents a new metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Annam Red-cheeked Squirrel" (ARCS), inspired by the foraging behavior of *Sciurus olivaceus*, commonly known as the Red-cheeked Squirrel. The algorithm leverages key aspects of squirrel foraging strategies – including caching, territory defense, and opportunistic searching – to develop a robust and efficient optimization technique. ARCS combines elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Simulated Annealing (SA) within a novel framework. Specifically, the algorithm employs a dynamic population size adaptation based on perceived resource availability, mimicking the squirrel's adjustments to food abundance. Furthermore, a "territory defense" mechanism is introduced, where particles compete for promising solutions, promoting exploration and preventing premature convergence. The performance of ARCS is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its competitive capability compared to established metaheuristic algorithms. The algorithm's adaptability and ability to handle complex search spaces make it a promising candidate for various real-world applications. The core mathematical formulation is detailed, focusing on the dynamic population size calculation, the territory defense mechanism, and the integration of PSO and SA components. The goal is to provide a clear and concise description of the algorithm's design and its potential for effective problem-solving.

title: Adaptive Neural Architecture Search with Evolutionary Strategies and Bayesian Optimization
abstract: Neural Architecture Search (NAS) has emerged as a powerful technique for automating the design of neural networks, offering the potential to discover architectures that outperform manually designed ones. However, traditional NAS methods often suffer from high computational cost, requiring extensive training and evaluation of numerous architectures. This paper proposes a novel adaptive architecture search framework that leverages the strengths of both evolutionary strategies (ES) and Bayesian optimization (BO) to address these limitations. The core idea is to dynamically adjust the search strategy based on the performance feedback received during the search process. ES is employed to explore the architecture space broadly, while BO is utilized to refine the search around promising regions identified by ES. This hybrid approach enables a more efficient and targeted exploration, ultimately leading to the discovery of high-performing architectures with reduced computational effort. The framework incorporates adaptive mutation rates in the ES component and utilizes a Gaussian Process (GP) model in the BO component to efficiently model the performance landscape. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this adaptive approach through simulations, showcasing its ability to converge to optimal or near-optimal architectures with significantly fewer evaluations compared to conventional NAS methods.

title: Title: Dynamic Phase Space Evolution in Complex Algorithms
abstract: This paper explores the application of dynamic phase space evolution to complex algorithms, offering a novel framework for automated optimization. Traditional algorithm analysis often relies on static evaluations, failing to capture the intricate dynamics of complex systems. We propose a system that continuously evaluates the algorithm's trajectory, dynamically adjusting parameters to achieve optimal performance. This approach moves beyond static analysis, enabling the discovery of optimal strategies through continuous adaptation. The core mechanism involves a system of iterative parameter adjustments, driven by the algorithm's trajectory, fostering a dynamic optimization process. The implications of this work are significant, potentially revolutionizing the design and optimization of complex computational systems across diverse domains.

title: Andean Swamp Rat Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the Andean Swamp Rat Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (ASIMA), designed to address complex optimization challenges. The algorithm's design is inspired by the foraging behavior of Andean Swamp Rats, particularly their adaptive movement strategies in complex and dynamic environments. ASIMA combines elements of particle swarm optimization (PSO) and simulated annealing (SA) with a novel adaptive exploration-exploitation mechanism mimicking the rat's navigation skills. The core innovation lies in a dynamically adjusted 'territory size' parameter, reflecting the rat's ability to adjust its search area based on encountered resources and obstacles. Mathematical formulations detailing the algorithm's key components, including the territory size adjustment, velocity update, and acceptance probability calculations, are provided. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time. Keywords: Metaheuristic Algorithm, Particle Swarm Optimization, Simulated Annealing, Adaptive Exploration, Adaptive Exploitation, Optimization, Complex Problems, Andean Swamp Rats.

title: Title: Topology-Based Optimization of Neural Network Weights
abstract: Topology-based optimization offers a novel approach to neural network weight optimization, moving beyond traditional gradient descent methods. This paper investigates the application of topological concepts – specifically, connected components, loops, and other structural properties – to identify and mitigate redundancy and instability within neural network weights. We propose a method for quantifying network topology and leveraging these measures to guide weight adjustments, resulting in improved robustness and generalization. The core claim is that applying topological principles can lead to more robust and adaptable neural network models.

title: Quantum Topological Information Cryptography
abstract: Quantum Topological Information Cryptography (QTIC) explores the potential of leveraging quantum phenomena, specifically quantum topology, to develop novel cryptographic techniques. This paper investigates the design and implementation of a QTIC system centered around the principles of quantum entanglement and topology, aiming to establish a fundamentally more secure communication paradigm compared to existing methods. We delve into the core mechanisms of the algorithm, focusing on the creation of a quantum key distribution (QKD) system, data encryption utilizing quantum mechanics, and a unique measurement procedure. The research highlights the advantages offered by quantum topology in enhancing security and introduces a new approach to data protection. This work presents a foundational investigation into the possibilities of QTIC, emphasizing its potential for advancements in cryptographic security.

title: ## American Polecat: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Adaptive Behavior of *Mustela americana*
abstract: This paper introduces American Polecat ( *Mustela americana* ), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging and territorial defense strategies observed in this North American mustelid. Unlike traditional metaheuristics which often rely on predefined parameters or complex evolutionary models, American Polecat mimics the polecat's dynamic approach to resource acquisition and conflict resolution. The algorithm leverages a combination of adaptive exploration and exploitation, represented by a 'territory' concept and a 'resource' assessment system. The core mechanism involves a dynamically adjusted search space based on perceived resource availability, utilizing a novel 'marking' strategy to avoid redundant exploration. We present the algorithm's theoretical foundation, its key components, and demonstrate its effectiveness through simulations on benchmark optimization problems, including the Rastrigin function and the Sphere function. Preliminary results indicate that American Polecat exhibits competitive performance compared to established metaheuristics like Genetic Algorithms and Particle Swarm Optimization, particularly in challenging landscapes with high dimensionality and complex fitness landscapes. Future research will focus on expanding the algorithm's applicability and incorporating real-world constraints.

title: Probabilistic Programming for Simulation-Based Discovery of Physical Laws
abstract: The process of discovering fundamental physical laws often relies heavily on theoretical modeling and, crucially, experimental observation and analysis. However, complex physical systems, particularly those with many interacting components or stochastic elements, pose a significant challenge. Traditional methods of analytical modeling can become intractable, and even numerical simulations can be computationally prohibitive, particularly when exploring a wide range of parameter spaces. This work proposes a novel approach leveraging probabilistic programming to automate the discovery of physical laws from simulation data. We demonstrate how probabilistic programming languages, such as Stan and PyMC3, can be used to represent physical systems as probabilistic models. Through repeated simulation runs, coupled with Bayesian inference, the model parameters are iteratively refined, effectively learning the governing laws. This process, driven by data-driven inference, offers a powerful alternative to manual model construction and parameter tuning, significantly accelerating the pace of scientific discovery. The core of this approach lies in the ability to efficiently explore high-dimensional parameter spaces and robustly estimate the relationships between simulation outputs and model parameters, leading to a more accurate representation of the underlying physical phenomena. The efficiency gains are substantial when compared to traditional methods, opening avenues for exploring systems previously considered intractable. ---

title: Altai Zokor: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Altai Zokor
abstract: This paper presents Altai Zokor, a novel metaheuristic algorithm designed to address complex optimization problems. The algorithm draws inspiration from the unique foraging behavior of the Altai Zokor, a resilient and adaptable animal found in the high-altitude regions of Central Asia. Altai Zokor's ability to navigate challenging terrains and efficiently locate scarce resources serves as the core principle behind the algorithm's design. The proposed approach utilizes a combination of adaptive mutation, a novel constriction heuristic, and a dynamic population size strategy to enhance exploration and exploitation capabilities. We demonstrate the efficacy of Altai Zokor through theoretical analysis and illustrate its performance on a range of benchmark problems, including the Rastrigin function, the Sphere function, and the Powell's test functions. The results demonstrate that Altai Zokor consistently achieves competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as the Genetic Algorithm and the Particle Swarm Optimization. Future research will focus on further refining the algorithm's parameters and exploring its application in real-world engineering and scientific domains.

title: ## White Egret-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (WEMOA)
abstract: This paper introduces the White Egret-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (WEMOA), a novel optimization approach motivated by the foraging behavior of the White Egret ( *Egretta alba*). White Egrets exhibit remarkable adaptability and efficiency in locating food sources, utilizing a combination of exploration and exploitation strategies. WEMOA leverages these traits by incorporating a dynamic exploration radius, a weighted average of global and local best solutions, and a mechanism for adjusting the search intensity based on the perceived 'richness' of the search space. The algorithm aims to improve upon existing metaheuristic methods by mimicking the bird's strategic decision-making process, particularly its ability to balance systematic searching with opportunistic responses to promising areas. This paper details the algorithm's theoretical framework, mathematical formulation, and an explanation of the design choices inspired by the observed behavior of White Egrets.

title: Agricola's Gracile Opossum: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Animal's Adaptive Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Agricola's Gracile Opossum (AGO), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of the Agricola's gracile opossum (*Didelphis virginiana*). The algorithm mimics the opossum's strategy of searching for food in a patchy environment, utilizing a combination of exploration and exploitation phases. AGO employs a population-based search, represented by a set of "caches" where each cache contains a potential solution. The algorithm dynamically adjusts the number of caches and their positions based on the environment's landscape, mimicking the opossum's selective caching strategy. A key component is the 'Cache Acceptance Probability' (CAP) which determines the likelihood of a new cache being created or an existing cache being discarded, influenced by the quality of solutions found in neighboring caches. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through a series of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and efficiency compared to established metaheuristic algorithms. The core idea is to create a dynamic landscape of solutions, forcing the search to adapt and converge towards optimal or near-optimal solutions. The algorithm's design prioritizes computational efficiency while maintaining robust performance across diverse problem types.

title: The Burrowing Optimization Algorithm: A Biomimetic Approach Inspired by Prairie Dog Behavior
abstract: This paper introduces the Burrowing Optimization Algorithm (BOA), a novel metaheuristic optimization technique inspired by the collective behavior of prairie dogs during burrow construction and territory defense. BOA mimics the iterative process of prairie dogs selecting, evaluating, and modifying potential burrow locations, incorporating concepts of spatial competition, resource allocation, and social signaling. The algorithm utilizes a multi-dimensional search space representing potential solutions, employing a 'burrow' concept to encapsulate and evolve candidate solutions. Key components include a 'stability' metric for evaluating solution quality, a 'pressure' mechanism simulating territorial competition, and a 'social influence' component mimicking prairie dog communication. The BOA aims to achieve robust and efficient convergence, particularly in complex, high-dimensional search landscapes. This paper details the algorithm's theoretical framework, operational rules, and discusses its potential applications in various optimization problems.

This paper investigates the design and implementation of a dynamic geometry mapping and optimization algorithm based on quantum topology, aiming to surpass traditional methods in complex systems. The core mechanism centers around employing dynamic geometric mapping to systematically explore and manipulate the system's geometry, driven by the inherent topological constraints. We present a framework for generating and applying such mappings, demonstrating its potential to achieve superior results in various optimization scenarios. The paper explores the advantages of this dynamic approach, including enhanced adaptability and the ability to navigate intricate geometries.

title: Alpine Musk Deer: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Behavior of Alpine Musk Deer
abstract: This paper presents Alpine Musk Deer (AMD), a new metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of the alpine musk deer ( *Moschus angustidens* ). The algorithm leverages the musk deer's ability to navigate complex, mountainous terrain and efficiently locate scarce food resources. AMD employs a novel combination of adaptive parameter control, a multi-dimensional exploration strategy, and a dynamic population structure to optimize solutions effectively. The core mechanism mimics the deer's movement pattern, incorporating elements of random walking, obstacle avoidance, and resource prioritization. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through a series of benchmark problems across diverse optimization landscapes, demonstrating its competitive capabilities compared to established metaheuristic techniques. We present detailed mathematical formulations for key components of AMD, including the adaptive step size calculation, the probability of movement, and the population density management. The results indicate that AMD offers a robust and efficient solution for a range of optimization problems, particularly those with complex, multimodal landscapes and sparse resource distributions. The algorithm's adaptive nature and exploration strategy contribute to its ability to escape local optima and converge towards global solutions.

title: Quantum States of Self-Adjustment
abstract: Quantum states exhibit a remarkable capacity for self-adjustment, a phenomenon central to the potential of quantum computing. This paper investigates the theoretical framework of self-adjusting quantum states, exploring a novel mechanism for dynamic state evolution driven by parameter adjustments. We argue that this self-adjustment process offers a pathway to optimize quantum computation, addressing limitations of static quantum algorithms. The core claim is that by employing a self-adjusting quantum state, we can achieve dynamic changes in the quantum system, ultimately enhancing efficiency.

title: Probability Distribution Dynamic Adjustment
abstract: This paper presents a novel dynamic adjustment algorithm for machine learning models, leveraging probability distributions to guide parameter optimization. The core principle is to dynamically adjust model parameters based on the predicted uncertainty associated with the model's output, mitigating the risk of overfitting and enhancing model generalization. The algorithm employs a probabilistic model to assess the likelihood of different parameter values, allowing for iterative refinement based on this assessment. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of experiments, showcasing superior performance compared to traditional optimization methods and highlighting the benefits of incorporating probability distributions.

title: A Self-Adaptive Multi-Learning Strategy Particle Swarm Optimizer for UWB Indoor Positioning Anchors Layout Optimization
abstract: Particle swarm optimization (PSO) is a widely used method for solving single-objective optimization problems. However, PSO suffers from diversity loss and premature convergence, leading to suboptimal performance in complex problems. To address these limitations, this paper introduces a novel self-adaptive multi-learning strategy PSO (SMLS-PSO) designed for real-parameter optimization tasks. SMLS-PSO integrates four distinct learning strategy-based PSO variants into a behavior pool and employs a new self-adaptive strategy selection mechanism. This mechanism dynamically chooses the most suitable learning strategy to update the velocities and positions of particles based on fitness information and payoff at different evolutionary stages. To enhance the performance of SMLS-PSO, three key improvements are incorporated: (1) a stagnation counter parameter to minimize wasted fitness evaluations; (2) a boundary symmetry mapping method to manage out-of-range searches; and (3) a Quasi-Newton local search operator to boost local exploitation capabilities. SMLS-PSO is first compared with four component PSO variants on 13 basic benchmark functions. Subsequently, SMLS-PSO is compared with eight state-of-the-art PSO variants on both 30D and 50D CEC2017 test suite problems. Experimental results indicate that SMLS-PSO statistically and significantly outperforms the compared algorithms on the majority of the test problems, showcasing its superior optimization capabilities. Finally, SMLS-PSO was applied to the optimization problem of UWB anchors layout, and it achieved a higher locatable space coverage rate and a better average HDOP value compared to the conventional layout scheme and other PSO variant optimization schemes.

title: On the Exploration and Exploitation Capabilities of Adaptive Differential Evolution: A Case Study Using JADE, L-SHADE, and jDElscop
abstract: Differential Evolution (DE) is one of the most successful population-based optimization algorithms, and numerous adaptive variants, such as JADE, L-SHADE, and jDElscop, have been proposed to improve its search performance. Although these methods consistently outperform classical DE variants, whether they genuinely improve the balance between exploration and exploitation remains largely unexamined, since prior evaluations relied on imprecise diversity-based measures. This paper presents a detailed study of DE variants using the recently proposed attraction basin-based measures that distinguish between different types of exploration (successful, failed, deceptive, and successful rejection) and exploitation (successful and unsuccessful). The exploration and exploitation behavior of JADE, L-SHADE, and jDElscop is compared with four classical DE strategies: DE/best/1/bin, DE/best/1/exp, DE/rand/1/bin, and DE/rand/1/exp. The results show that adaptive DE variants prolong the exploration phase and improve the balance between successful and unsuccessful exploitation compared with the classical strategies, though each achieves this through a distinct mechanism. The presented findings improve the understanding of adaptive DE search behavior and demonstrate the usefulness of attraction basin-based measures for analyzing evolutionary optimization algorithms.

title: The Evolution of Open Licensing in the CIS and the Application of Artificial Intelligence Technologies to Processing Scientific and Technical Information
abstract: Introduction . Open licenses have become the foundation of the Open Access movement and open science. However, classic licenses, including the GNU GPL and the Creative Commons (CC) family, do not address the specifics of using works as training data for AI, nor do they regulate the legal status of neural network weights and the output data generated by models. Aim . To analyze the evolution of open licensing in the CIS member states, identify the legal and practical aspects of applying artificial intelligence (AI) technologies to process scientific and technical information (STI) on leading regional platforms, and develop recommendations for adapting licensing mechanisms to the tasks of automatic abstracting, annotation, and thematic structuring. Materials and Methods . The study is based on a comparative legal analysis of the national legislation of the Russian Federation, the Republic of Belarus, the Republic of Kazakhstan, and Ukraine regarding the regulation of open licenses. A review of the practical implementation of AI technologies (neurosearch, automatic classification, text summarization) on the platforms of the Scientific Electronic Library eLibrary, the National Electronic Library of the National Library of the Russian Academy of Sciences, the All-Russian Scientific and Technical Library of the Russian Academy of Sciences, the State Public Scientific and Technical Library of Russia, and the United Institute of Informatics and Problems of the National Academy of Sciences of Belarus was conducted. An analysis of the compatibility of Creative Commons (CC) licenses and specialized AI licenses (OpenMDW, RAIL) with machine learning tasks on NTI datasets was conducted. Results . Heterogeneity of the legal regulation of open licenses in the CIS was established: the most developed systems are in Russia (Articles 1286.1 and 1368 of the Civil Code of the Russian Federation), Belarus (Article 45 of Law No. 262-Z), and Kazakhstan (Digital Code of 2026). It was found that platforms are actively implementing AI, but licensing restrictions create legal barriers to automated processing. Unresolved issues include the legal status of datasets, neural network model weights, and model outputs, as well as the lack of exceptions for text and data mining (TDM) in CIS legislation. It was shown that CC BY-licensed collections and public domain works are most suitable for creating open datasets. Conclusion. To legally use AI in processing NTI, libraries and information centers are recommended to primarily use CC BY-licensed documents, comply with ND and NC restrictions, and label automatically generated content. Harmonization of CIS legislation, adaptation of specialized AI licenses to regional practices, and the development of a standard open licensing policy for automated processing of NTI at the level of the State Public Scientific and Technical Library of Russia are advisable.

title: Explainable Machine Learning untuk Mendukung Pengambilan Keputusan yang Adil dan Transparan
abstract: The use of machine learning to support decision-making is increasingly widespread in various fields. However, many machine learning models are highly complex, making their decision-making processes difficult to understand. This situation has the potential to raise issues related to transparency, accountability, and fairness in data-driven decisions. Therefore, an approach is needed that can explain how the model works without compromising its predictive value. This research aims to examine the application of explainable machine learning as an approach to supporting fair and transparent decision-making. The research method involves building a machine learning model using commonly used algorithms and then applying explainability techniques to analyze the contribution of each feature to the prediction results. Model evaluation focuses not only on predictive performance but also on the model's interpretability in explaining the resulting decisions. The analysis shows that the application of explainable machine learning can provide a better understanding of the model's decision-making process and help identify significantly influential factors. This approach enables users to evaluate model decisions more rationally and responsibly. Thus, explainable machine learning has the potential to become a critical component in the development of machine learning-based decision support systems that emphasize fairness and transparency.

title: Tourism Route Optimization Based on the Travelling Salesman Problem Using Ant Colony Optimization in the Banyumas and Purbalingga Regions
abstract: Tourism route planning requires an efficient visiting sequence to reduce travel distance and transportation costs. When multiple tourist destinations must be visited in a single trip, the route-planning problem can be formulated as a Travelling Salesman Problem (TSP). This study implements Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) to determine an efficient route among 12 tourist destinations in Banyumas and Purbalingga. The destinations were represented as nodes in a weighted graph, while the travel distance between each pair of destinations was used as the edge weight. The algorithm constructed candidate routes using probabilistic selection and updated pheromone values based on route quality. Three pheromone evaporation rates, namely ρ=0.3, ρ=0.5, and ρ=0.7, were evaluated. The shortest route obtained in the first iteration was W1–W3–W2–W4–W8–W9–W7–W10–W11–W12–W6–W5–W1, with a total distance of 109.0 km. After pheromone updating, the pheromone levels on the shortest-route edges were 0.016174, 0.014174, and 0.012174 for evaporation rates of 0.3, 0.5, and 0.7, respectively. These results show that the evaporation rate directly affects pheromone retention, with a lower evaporation rate maintaining stronger pheromone information on the selected route. The study demonstrates that ACO can generate an efficient tourism route and provides a computational basis for developing a tourism route decision-support system.

title: EARTHQUAKE CLUSTER MAPPING IN ACEH PROVINCE: AN ORDERING POINTS TO IDENTIFY THE CLUSTERING STRUCTURE (OPTICS) CLUSTERING APPROACH
abstract: Indonesia is known as a disaster-prone region. Located on the Pacific Ring of Fire, it is one of the countries most susceptible to various types of natural disasters. The province of Aceh is one of the regions in Indonesia that frequently experiences earthquakes due to its geographical location in a highly seismically active area. Therefore, an analysis of earthquake data clustering in the province of Aceh is necessary. The aim of this research is to determine earthquake clusters, which can be used for disaster mitigation and prevention measures. This research begins with examining the distribution pattern of data through a scatterplot. If the data distribution pattern shows varying density levels, then a clustering analysis using Ordering Points to Identify the Clustering Structure (OPTICS) is conducted. In the OPTICS algorithm, two parameters are required before clustering: minimum points (MinPts) and xi. The clustering results are evaluated using the silhouette coefficient (SC). Further data exploration is carried out by: (1) reducing the MinPts value, (2) clustering based on the supremum of the SC, and (3) identifying earthquake events with potential tsunami risks. The purpose of this data exploration is to increase the number of clusters formed while still considering the SC value limit, thus expanding the regions identified as earthquake-prone. The best clustering results are determined by comparing the obtained clusters. The best clustering result was found at MinPts = 20 and xi = 0.05, forming 4 clusters with a silhouette coefficient value of 0.72, indicating a strong cluster structure. This information is expected to benefit the public by raising awareness of earthquake-prone areas.

title: Reasoning-Aware Compression: Identifying and Protecting Vulnerable Reasoning Circuits for Energy-Efficient LLM Deployment
abstract: Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) impose substantial energy costs during deployment, yet current compression methods apply uniform quantization across all components, risking damage to critical reasoning circuits. We present a reasoning-aware compression framework that benchmarks quantization conditions across five reasoning benchmarks, GSM8K, FOLIO, MATH-500, ProofWriter, and MuSiQue, with hardware-level GPU energy measurement; profiles per-module INT4 vulnerability across all 196-224 (layer, projection) pairs via a perturbation sweep on a held-out calibration split, then selectively restores the most sensitive circuits to FP16. Three findings emerge. First, INT4 quantization can increase energy by extending reasoning chains; a 25% power reduction becomes a net energy increase on GSM8K. Second, vulnerability is task-dependent: attention projections are more critical for mathematical reasoning, and sensitivity patterns differ by architecture in logical inference. Third, selective compression achieves Pareto-optimal points inaccessible to uniform methods: R1-Qwen-7B Top-10% on ProofWriter gains +12 pp over FP16 at -9.7% energy, validated on held-out data across five reasoning benchmarks.

title: MusGU+: Toward a Musician-Centered Evaluation Framework and Discovery Tool for Generative Music AI
abstract: Generative music systems are increasingly presented as tools that democratize music creation, yet their practical suitability for musicians remains underexplored. Prior work includes openness-focused evaluation frameworks, such as MusGO (Music-Generative Open AI), as well as qualitative studies of musicians' experiences with generative systems. However, these approaches do not support systematic comparison or early-stage discovery of models for creative use. Motivated by such limitations, we introduce MusGU+, a musician-centered evaluation framework organized around three dimensions: Adaptability, Usability, and Controllability. Together, these capture whether a model can be feasibly trained or fine-tuned on personal data, integrated into real-world music workflows, and controlled in musically meaningful ways. We evaluate 10 representative generative music systems and present an interactive discovery tool that enables musicians to explore and filter models according to these criteria. While MusGO remains valuable for promoting responsible research practices, MusGU+ supports informed selection and practical adoption of generative systems by musicians.

title: Liquid Gated Attention
abstract: Real-world time series often exhibit irregular sampling and extended temporal horizons, requiring models to capture continuous-time dynamics across arbitrary intervals without prohibitive scaling costs. Discrete-time methods collapse variable time intervals into static positional steps; solver-dependent continuous-time models preserve temporal structure but rely on sequential integration, precluding parallelization; and solver-free approximations avoid this cost yet none couples observed time intervals with input-driven state modulation. We propose Liquid Gated Attention (LGA), a solver-free parallel temporal operator. By parameterizing an input-driven gating mechanism with observed time intervals, LGA introduces a continuous-time inductive bias and formulates hidden state evolution as a fast-weight associative memory, enabling parallel computation across the temporal dimension. Using matrix associativity in non-causal encoding and a prefix scan in causal encoding, LGA attains linear temporal complexity in sequence length in both modes. A sequence-level normalization bounds cumulative temporal decay for stable long-horizon optimization. Building on LGA, we instantiate LFormer, a modular backbone for continuous-time representation learning. Across six tasks and sixteen datasets spanning up to 17,984 steps, LFormer demonstrates long-range dependency modeling, fine-grained state tracking, and trajectory reconstruction from sparse and noisy observations, while delivering competitive performance against state-of-the-art discrete-time and continuous-time baselines with linear scaling efficiency.

title: Bounds on the Posterior-to-Prior Ratios for Inclusion Belief under Bounded Differential Privacy
abstract: Differential privacy has become the standard for generating privacy-protected data releases. However, differential privacy does not translate intuitively to disclosure risk. In particular, it remains unclear how much an adversary's belief about an individual's inclusion in a dataset can change after observing a protected release. To address this question, we derive upper and lower bounds on the posterior-to-prior ratios of inclusion beliefs under bounded probabilistic and approximate differential privacy. By assuming a worst-case adversary with all-but-one auxiliary information, i.e., knowledge of all except for one of the participants in a dataset, we obtain bounds that apply to any adversary. Because these bounds may fail with non-zero probability, we study the corresponding failure probability for the Gaussian mechanism. We derive a theoretical upper limit on this probability and compare it with Monte Carlo estimates across a wide range of parameter settings. The observed failure rate is several orders of magnitude smaller than its theoretical upper limit, indicating that the latter is highly conservative. These findings suggest that the inferential privacy guarantees provided by differentially private mechanisms may be substantially stronger in practice than what is implied by the theoretical upper limit.

title: Transparency, Authenticity, and Accountability: An Ethical Frame for AI Avatar Use in Digital Marketing
abstract: Nowadays, any brand can generate an AI avatar to interact with its customers, or a synthetic brand representative, to communicate key messages, all in a matter of hours at minimal cost. The increased accessibility of AI generative entities is transforming digital marketing at a pace that can’t keep up with ethical regulatory frameworks. We examine three recurring issues in the literature: limited transparency, simulated authenticity, and diffused accountability, based on 35 peer-reviewed studies published between 2020 and 2026. We maintain that these issues cannot be addressed separately because a brand can be compliant with transparency policies and, at the same time, take advantage of parasocial attachment, and the involved parties can establish conduct policies without accountability for the avatar-consumer relationship. Therefore, we propose an integrated ethical framework in which transparency, authenticity, and accountability are interconnected obligations that define the ethical conditions for AI avatars' responsible and sustainable marketing practices.

title: Implementasi Transformer-Based LLM Chatbot Berbasis AI pada Website Rekrutment PT Patra Drilling Contractor
abstract: Proses rekrutmen sebelumnya di PT Patra Drilling Contractor masih dilakukan secara manual menggunakan formulir standar dan Google Form, sehingga menimbulkan beberapa kendala signifikan. Di antara kendala tersebut adalah tingginya volume pertanyaan dari kandidat mengenai proses rekrutmen yang menambah beban kerja Tim Human Capital (HC), penumpukan pertanyaan pelamar melalui email yang memaksa Tim HC membentuk grup WhatsApp tambahan untuk diseminasi informasi, serta keharusan Tim HC untuk membalas secara manual setiap pertanyaan karena belum tersedianya sistem otomatis dan real-time. Penelitian ini bertujuan merancang dan membangun website karir PT Patra Drilling Contractor yang dilengkapi chatbot berbasis AI dengan Transformer-Based Large Language Model (LLM) sebagai solusi atas permasalahan tersebut. Pengembangan sistem menggunakan metode Agile melalui tiga sprint iteratif: perancangan website dan database rekrutmen, pengembangan chatbot umum, dan pengembangan chatbot personal. Model AI yang diimplementasikan adalah Natural Language Processing berbasis Transformer-Based LLM dengan mekanisme Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) yang diintegrasikan melalui Groq API serta rule-based keyword matching untuk klasifikasi intent. Sistem chatbot terdiri dari dua jenis: chatbot umum yang dapat diakses tanpa login untuk menjawab pertanyaan seputar lowongan dan prosedur melamar, serta chatbot personal yang dapat diakses setelah login untuk memberikan rekomendasi posisi dan informasi status lamaran secara personal. Hasil pengujian fungsional menggunakan metode Blackbox dan Whitebox Testing menunjukkan seluruh jalur pemrosesan utama pada komponen chatbot AI berhasil berjalan sesuai spesifikasi rancangan, dan hasil User Acceptance Testing (UAT) mencapai tingkat keberhasilan 100%.

title: On Regularization of Deep Learning Models Based on Information Geometry
abstract: This paper explores a novel approach to regularization of deep learning models by leveraging the principles of information geometry. We introduce a framework wherein the model parameters are mapped into an information geometric space, representing the intrinsic geometry of the model's probability distribution. By optimizing the model's distribution within this intrinsic space, we aim to improve the model's generalization ability. The core idea is to move beyond traditional regularization techniques, which often rely on empirical loss functions, and to ground the regularization process in the inherent structure of the data manifold. This work provides a theoretical foundation and a practical method for regularizing deep learning models, offering a potentially significant improvement in their performance. The presented methodology offers a new perspective on model regularization, emphasizing the intrinsic geometry of learned representations. ---

title: Topological Protection of Quantum Error Correction
abstract: This paper investigates the application of topological protection to enhance quantum error correction, ultimately aiming for increased reliability in quantum information transmission and storage. The core concept revolves around encoding quantum bits (qubits) within topological defects, specifically leveraging the robust protection offered by these defects against local disturbances. We explore theoretical frameworks where topological protection fundamentally alters the error correction landscape, moving beyond traditional approaches reliant on local control and measurement. The study details how the inherent symmetries and conserved quantities associated with topological defects create a resilient environment for qubits, effectively mitigating the detrimental effects of decoherence and noise. Mathematical models are presented to illustrate the principles of topological error correction, including the concept of topological codes and their ability to detect and correct errors without directly measuring the qubits themselves. The paper concludes with a discussion on the challenges and future directions in realizing practical topological quantum computers, emphasizing the need for controlled manipulation and characterization of topological defects.

title: Governed Software Evolution: Embedded Engineering Agents and the Curation of User-Originated Variability in Enterprise Applications
abstract: Enterprise applications are extended through a ticket queue: the people who hold the intent (domain experts) are separated from the people who hold the keys (developers) by a chain of translation steps that is slow, lossy, and economically unable to serve the long tail of small, team-specific needs. LLM-based coding agents make it technically feasible to collapse that chain by embedding an engineering capability inside the application itself, so that a procurement manager or a sales lead can extend the product by describing what they need. We argue that this is not primarily a code-generation problem but a variability-management problem, and that it breaks the central assumption of software product-line engineering: that variation points are declared at design time by an architect and that tenants configure within them. When extensions are generated bottom-up by thousands of domain experts at runtime, variation becomes unbounded and unanticipated, and the well-known failure mode of variant explosion is no longer a modelling risk but an operational certainty unless the organisation curates continuously. This position paper (i) identifies the assumption that agentic runtime extension breaks, (ii) proposes a reference architecture in which extensions are generated by an embedded agent, isolated per user, and bound to the host through a versioned extension contract and a capability-based permission model, (iii) proposes a tiered promotion pipeline — personal, team, enterprise — in which variability management becomes a continuous curation problem gated by an enterprise platform team, and (iv) lays out an evaluation design and the open problems, including semantic correctness against unstated intent, which we treat as a declared limitation rather than a solved problem. We position the proposal against end-user software engineering, self-evolving agents, agentic software engineering, and the citizen-development governance models already deployed in industry, and we are explicit about what is synthesis and what is new. Position/vision paper. No system has been implemented, and no empirical results are reported. The author used an AI assistant for drafting, literature search, and revision. All claims, designs, analyses, and citations were reviewed and verified by the author, who takes full responsibility for the content.

title: Adaptive Quantum Environment Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This paper introduces an adaptive quantum environment reinforcement learning framework, aiming to achieve precise modeling and prediction of quantum system behavior. Traditional reinforcement learning relies on static environments, limiting its applicability to complex systems. Our proposed method dynamically adjusts the quantum environment to guide the system towards desired states, offering a significant improvement in performance compared to conventional approaches. We detail the core mechanism, utilizing quantum environment dynamics to create a self-optimizing learning process. The study addresses the limitations of traditional reinforcement learning by incorporating a dynamic environment, leading to enhanced precision and adaptability. This work presents a novel framework with potential applications in diverse quantum computing tasks and simulations.

title: Algorithmic Quantum State Exploration with Hybrid Search
abstract: Quantum state exploration is a fundamental challenge in quantum computing, requiring the efficient discovery of complex quantum states. Traditional approaches often struggle with the inherent complexity of these spaces, limiting the speed and scope of the search process. This paper introduces an algorithmic quantum state exploration method that leverages the strengths of both classical and quantum search algorithms, resulting in a significant increase in speed and efficiency. The core of this approach is a novel "Hybrid Quantum Search Algorithm," which strategically combines classical search to guide initial exploration with quantum search for probing areas of interest. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this method through a series of simulations and analyses, showcasing a substantial improvement in the speed of finding specific quantum states compared to existing techniques. This work represents a significant advancement in quantum state exploration, offering a promising pathway toward broader and more efficient discovery of quantum states.

title: Topological Quantum Error Correction
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to Quantum Error Correction (QEC) based on topological quantum structures. Traditional QEC methods often rely on measurement, which introduces errors. We propose a new algorithm that leverages the inherent properties of quantum error correction to construct a robust and efficient correction scheme. The core of this approach is the design of a topological structure that protects quantum information from local errors. This structure, when manipulated, effectively mitigates the propagation of quantum information errors, leading to improved performance and resilience. The algorithm's novelty lies in its fundamental shift towards exploiting the quantum properties of the structure itself rather than relying on post-processing measurements. We analyze the algorithm's performance and demonstrate its potential for significantly enhanced error correction capabilities compared to existing techniques.
